As a Property Manager based in the Greater Phoenix area, you'll carry a portfolio that spans state lines and grows over time. The skills you'll use most are expectation management, systems thinking, and cross-functional coordination. Leasing, R&M, resident services, and accounting all run through you, not because you're executing every task yourself, but because you're the owner of the outcome and the investor's primary point of contact.

The investor relationship here is closer to an asset manager relationship than a traditional PM-owner dynamic. You'll be tracking performance against each investor's specific goals and objectives, resolving complex issues at the root level rather than patching them repeatedly, and coordinating with Roofstock's internal departments and centralized teams to get things done. Strong virtual relationship skills matter as much as operational knowledge. Most of your investor interactions won't happen in person.

  • Active Arizona Real Estate License required
  • 3 or more years in residential or commercial property management or real estate operations
  • Direct experience working with property ownership, preferred
  • Cost and revenue management experience, highly preferred
  • Comfort working across multiple PM software platforms
  • Bachelor's degree in business or related field, or equivalent experience
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation; minimum 10% local travel

The SFR Context Worth Understanding

Managing scattered-site single-family rentals at volume is genuinely different from managing a 200-unit garden-style community. There's no on-site team to absorb the daily friction. Turns happen one house at a time across multiple zip codes. Delinquency and maintenance coordination require tighter vendor relationships and faster individual decisions. The upside is that you're working with a platform built specifically for this asset class, with proprietary technology and centralized support teams designed to handle volume. The learning curve is real, but so is the infrastructure behind you.

Roofstock has grown through acquisitions of tools covering financial and asset management, tenant screening, and property management software for both retail and institutional investors. More recently, the company expanded into short-term rental management. That breadth means this role sits inside a company that is still evolving its own operating model, which suits someone who genuinely prefers building processes over inheriting them.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The PMs who thrive here tend to be people who treat their portfolio like a business they personally own. Investor communication that's proactive rather than reactive, task follow-through without hand-holding, and the ability to give honest, useful feedback on software and process changes without waiting to be asked. We've seen plenty of experienced PMs struggle in remote, tech-forward environments because they're accustomed to solving problems by walking down a hallway. If your default is to open a ticket and follow up, you'll do fine here. If you need in-person structure to stay organized, this one will be a grind.

Base salary for this position is $70,000 annually, with bonus eligibility tied to performance objectives. The role is fully remote within the Greater Phoenix area.

greenhouse_8541741002.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_8541741002.location: The Republic at Lubbock, Lubbock, Texas, United States
greenhouse_8541741002.rewritten_description:
The Republic at Lubbock is a student housing community, and this Assistant Property Manager role sits right at the center of its day-to-day operation. You'll work alongside the General Manager to keep the property running on all fronts: leasing, resident accounts, facilities, staff, and financials. When the GM is out, you run the show.

The work is concrete and varied. On a given day you might be auditing accounts receivable, walking vacant units to prep a punch list before turn season, handling an escalated resident complaint, and then pulling weekly market surveys to see where your concessions stand against competitors. Student housing moves fast, and the annual turn cycle is its own event. You'll help plan and execute it, which means coordinating room assignments, move-ins, and move-outs across a large volume of beds in a compressed window. If you've done a student housing turn before, you know what that takes. If you haven't, be ready to learn quickly.

On the financial side, you'll keep delinquency under 2% at month end, post damage charges from quarterly inspections, assist with month-end reporting, and make sure utility billing is accurate. Entrata experience is a plus here since that's the preferred platform. You'll also help enforce late fees and NSF policies and process final billing or refunds at move-out.

Staff development is part of the job too. You'll coach team members, help with hiring, and make sure everyone is trained on Fair Housing and company policies. You'll also manage the on-call schedule, which means you'll occasionally field after-hours situations yourself.

What the role requires

  • At least one year of experience in property management or a residential living community
  • Comfort with property management software, Entrata preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Close attention to detail, especially with accounts and compliance
  • Ability to step into the GM role when needed
  • Flexibility for non-standard hours during peak periods and emergencies

One thing worth knowing about student housing specifically: the resident base turns over almost entirely every 12 months. That keeps leasing and renewal activity constant and means your customer experience work never really stops. Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be organized under pressure and genuinely good at shifting between administrative work and direct resident interaction without losing focus on either. If you've managed delinquency and handled lease-up traffic simultaneously, that background translates well here.

This role is on-site at The Republic at Lubbock. Scion is one of the larger operators in the student housing space, so there's real room to grow into a General Manager position from here.

greenhouse_7728548003.rewritten_description:
It's 9 a.m. and you're already cross-referencing a delinquency report from one neighborhood while a Home Base Coordinator at another property is on the phone waiting for your sign-off on a move-in file. This is a normal Tuesday for a Home Base Supervisor at Prometheus.

Prometheus Real Estate Group has been quietly building one of the Bay Area's most respected apartment portfolios since 1965. With more than 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle, this is a company that owns and operates for the long term. They're vertically integrated, which means acquisitions, development, renovations, and operations all live under one roof. For the people who work here, that structure creates real depth of career exposure. It also means the Home Base Supervisor role touches more of the business than a comparable title at a third-party management company ever would.

What This Role Actually Involves

The title is "Home Base Supervisor," and Prometheus uses it deliberately. These aren't traditional administrative leads. The role spans multiple properties and carries genuine leadership weight. On any given day, you're auditing lease documentation for accuracy and fair housing compliance, approving or flagging move-in and renewal files, reviewing delinquency reports, and supporting the team through the full leasing cycle from application verification through resident qualification. When evictions are necessary, you help coordinate that process in compliance with legal direction and court orders.

Managing people is a real part of this job. You'll hire, train, and direct Home Base Coordinators, conduct performance reviews, handle complaints, and keep the administrative side of multiple properties running accurately. That means holding people accountable while also being someone they can bring problems to.

The cross-departmental piece is equally important. You'll work regularly with property management, operations, accounting, and neighborhood operations teams to resolve issues that don't fit neatly into one box. Prometheus also values people who notice when a process isn't working and say so. Suggesting practical policy improvements is an explicit part of the job.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least three years of property management experience, with at least two years in a supervisory capacity
  • Working knowledge of California housing rental laws, fair housing requirements, and lease documentation
  • Comfort with bookkeeping-level detail: delinquency tracking, rent collection oversight, and audit-readiness
  • A high school diploma or GED at minimum; a bachelor's degree is preferred
  • Ability to travel between properties as business needs require

The candidates who do best here aren't just organized. They're people who can read a tense situation with a resident or a struggling team member and respond with both firmness and fairness. Silicon Valley properties attract a demanding resident base, and the administrative layer of leasing operations leaves little room for documentation errors. Strong candidates bring both the interpersonal steadiness and the detail orientation to handle that combination without burning out.

Compensation runs from $39.25 to $45.00 per hour, with a discretionary annual bonus and additional incentives including referral, training coach, and lease-up bonuses. Prometheus covers 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for eligible employees and dependents, and offers a 401(k) with employer matching.

greenhouse_4241503009.location: Lorrel Apartments - 3465 Sandler Blvd - Little River, SC - 29566
greenhouse_4241503009.rewritten_description:
This role calls on two skill sets equally: leasing ability and financial accountability. If you're stronger in one than the other, this job will push you to close the gap. That's not a drawback. It's how you grow toward a Community Manager seat.

The Skills This Role Runs On

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, work incoming leads, process applications, and push renewals. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which means writing posts that actually reflect the property rather than generic filler. Keeping common areas and the leasing office in top condition falls under your watch too.

On the financial side, you'll handle rent collection, payment posting, and check scanning daily. You'll run ledger reviews to catch billing errors before they become disputes. Delinquency follow-up is a real part of the job: weekly calls, documentation, and coordinating eviction procedures when it gets to that point. You'll also assist with reporting for the Community Manager and regional leadership.

The role requires you to cover for the Community Manager when they're out. That means making decisions, keeping the team focused, and maintaining resident service without a pause. If you've had that experience before, even briefly, it matters here.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical day moves between the leasing office and the desk. You might start the morning reviewing delinquency reports and making follow-up calls, then shift to showing units to prospects in the afternoon. Resident concerns come in throughout the day and most require de-escalation before resolution. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to hold the 40-hour line. Some evenings and weekends come up for resident events.

Hawthorne expects you to read financial reports and make judgment calls within budget constraints, not just execute tasks. If numbers feel uncomfortable, that's worth addressing before you apply.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Two years of property management experience is preferred, along with at least six months in an assistant-level role. A CALP accreditation is a plus. But beyond credentials, the candidates who do well here are the ones who can hold a professional tone during a difficult resident conversation and still close a lease an hour later. Those two things don't always coexist naturally. The ones who make it work tend to move up.

Hawthorne's Career Path Program is a real structure, not a tagline. Assistant Community Manager to Community Manager is the standard trajectory here, backed by internal learning and development resources. Monthly leasing and renewal commissions plus quarterly performance bonuses supplement the hourly base pay.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months in an assistant community manager role preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP accreditation is a plus

greenhouse_4242032009.title: Market Maintenance Manager II
greenhouse_4242032009.rewritten_description:
Maintenance Manager roles come in a few varieties. Some are reactive, running from work order to work order with no real system behind them. This one at John M. Corcoran & Company is structured differently. You're overseeing the full physical operation of a residential community in Walpole, MA, which means you're managing the work, the people doing it, and the budget that pays for it.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Day to day, you'll own the maintenance workflow: work orders, unit turns, preventive maintenance scheduling, and property inspections. You'll supervise a team that includes maintenance techs, janitorial, and grounds staff, so your leadership style matters as much as your technical knowledge. Coordinating move-in readiness with the management team means you're also a key link between the maintenance side and the leasing side. Units need to be make-ready on time and to standard, and that's on you to track and deliver.

You'll manage vendor relationships, maintain purchase orders, and keep supply costs inside budget guidelines. You'll also carry an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That's worth naming plainly: this isn't a purely 8-to-4:30 job, even if most weeks feel like one.

  • 3+ years of trade or general building maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of electrical, mechanical, and building systems
  • Strong organizational and communication skills, with real supervisory experience
  • Ability to follow safety procedures and enforce company policies with the team
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Where This Role Builds Toward

The Maintenance Manager II designation signals that JMC uses a tiered structure, which matters for your career. Performing well here, specifically on budget adherence, turn efficiency, and team development, typically positions someone for a Regional Maintenance Director track or a multi-site oversight role as a portfolio grows. The skills you sharpen here (vendor management, capex planning, preventive maintenance programs) transfer directly to larger portfolios and higher-complexity assets. JMC has been operating in New England since 1951 and has a track record of promoting from within over the long term, which makes this a reasonable place to think about compounding your career rather than just landing a job.

Technical competency gets you in the door. What actually sets strong candidates apart in a supervisory maintenance role is the ability to build a team culture around accountability and quality without micromanaging. If you've run a tight preventive maintenance program that reduced emergency calls, or coached junior techs into reliable contributors, those specifics are worth highlighting when you apply. greenhouse_5214116008.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_5214116008.rewritten_description:
It's a Saturday morning, 9 a.m. sharp, and you've got two back-to-back tours booked before lunch. You pull up the CRM, confirm your guest cards are current, do a quick walk of the model and a vacant unit on the punch list from yesterday, and you're ready. That's the rhythm of this role at Ackermann Group, and if that kind of structured, people-centered pace appeals to you, it's worth reading on.

The Role

Ackermann Group has been developing and managing residential communities across the Midwest since 1938, and their Columbus-area portfolio reflects that long institutional history. They're hiring a full-time Leasing Consultant to represent their communities to prospective residents, maintain occupancy, and serve as a daily point of contact for current residents.

The core of the job is converting traffic into leases. That means greeting prospects, conducting tours, building genuine rapport quickly, and following through on every step of the leasing process, from the initial guest card to lease preparation and move-in documentation. You'll work in Yardi Voyager and Rent Cafe to track prospects, log interactions, and schedule follow-ups, and you'll be expected to keep that data clean and current.

Beyond leasing, this position carries real operational weight. You'll do routine inspections of units and common areas, flag anything that isn't market-ready, handle minor tidying yourself, and coordinate with the maintenance team on anything more involved. Resident service requests you receive get documented and routed appropriately. When resident concerns come up, the expectation is that you take initiative rather than waiting for direction.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., with rotating Saturdays from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. You'll also participate in after-hours resident events periodically and may support community outreach efforts.

What Ackermann Is Looking For

  • Prior customer service experience, required. Leasing or sales background, strongly preferred
  • Comfort with property management software, specifically Yardi Voyager and Rent Cafe. Microsoft Office proficiency expected
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build trust with prospective residents in a short window
  • Ability to work as part of a close-knit site team, including maintenance staff and a Community Manager
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Columbus is a competitive multifamily market, with consistent population growth driven by Ohio State, a diversifying tech and healthcare employment base, and steady in-migration from other Midwest metros. That means prospects often have real choices, and the leasing consultants who perform best here are the ones who know their product and their submarket well enough to make a clear, honest case for why this community fits. Generic sales energy doesn't close leases in a market with real options. Specific, informed conversations do.

Compensation includes an hourly rate plus commission on new and renewed leases. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company match, paid time off, a birthday holiday, an employee rent discount at Ackermann communities, and access to career coaching and development resources.

greenhouse_5214100008.title: Leasing Consultant - The Coleman
greenhouse_5214100008.rewritten_description:
The Coleman is a 256-unit community in Canal Winchester, Ohio, and Ackermann Group is adding a full-time Leasing Consultant to the team there. Ackermann has been operating in the Midwest since 1938, so this isn't a startup operation. There's process, structure, and a track record behind it.

The core of the job is converting traffic into signed leases. That means greeting prospects, running tours, logging guest cards accurately, preparing lease paperwork, and following up with enough consistency that your traffic-to-lease ratio stays where it needs to be. You'll also be the first voice residents hear when something comes up, and your ability to triage those calls matters. Simple issues get handled on the spot. Complex ones go to the right person without delay. That responsiveness is a direct driver of renewal rates and online reputation, both of which show up in NOI over time.

Routine unit and campus inspections are part of the role too. If something looks off during a walk, you either remedy it yourself or get maintenance moving. Market readiness isn't just the maintenance team's job. A leasing consultant who spots a punch list item before a tour saves a lease that might otherwise walk out the door.

You'll work in Yardi Voyager and Rent Café, tracking prospect interactions, scheduling appointments, and pulling reports. Accurate data entry isn't glamorous, but a guest card with missing fields or a follow-up that never got logged is a prospect that disappears. The administrative side of this role has real consequences for occupancy.

Ackermann also expects this person to stay current on the local rental market. Knowing what comparable communities are offering in terms of concessions and pricing gives you a sharper sales approach and makes you more credible in the leasing office.

One thing worth knowing about leasing consultant roles at conventional communities like this one: the skills you build here, specifically traffic management, CRM discipline, fair housing compliance, and resident relations, are the same skills that move people into assistant manager and community manager positions. Strong leasing consultants who understand their property's data tend to get noticed.

What Ackermann is looking for

  • Prior customer service experience (required); leasing or sales background is a strong plus
  • Comfort with Yardi Voyager, Rent Café, and CRM tools (preferred)
  • Solid written and verbal communication skills with an ability to build rapport quickly
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm, plus rotating Saturdays, 9am to 4pm
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Ability to work as part of a coordinated on-site team

Compensation includes an hourly rate plus commission on new and renewed leases, health benefits, 401k with company match, paid time off, an employee rent discount, and access to career coaching. The birthday PTO is a small thing, but it's the kind of detail that reflects how Ackermann thinks about its people.

greenhouse_7908336.title: Floating Maintenance Technician (Barrington Park & Fairfax Square)
greenhouse_7908336.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work is fundamentally a people skill dressed in a tool belt. You're solving problems under time pressure, communicating with residents who may be frustrated, coordinating with vendors who need clear direction, and keeping two property teams informed simultaneously. That's the real job description for a Floating Maintenance Technician at Van Metre, splitting time between Barrington Park Apartments in Manassas and Fairfax Square Apartments in Fairfax.

The Skills This Role Relies On

The technical side matters, of course. You'll need hands-on experience with appliance repair, plumbing, electrical work, and a working knowledge of HVAC and electrical circuitry. EPA certification is preferred, and you should already be current on OSHA and general building safety standards. Bringing your own basic tools is expected.

But the skill that separates a good floating tech from a great one is adaptability. Monday through Wednesday you're at Barrington Park; Thursday and Friday you're at Fairfax Square. Each property has its own Service Manager, its own quirks, its own recurring issues, and its own residents. You don't get the luxury of one routine. You have to read a new environment quickly, pick up where things left off, and build enough trust with two separate teams that communication stays tight even when you're not on site.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

Daily property walks to catch curb appeal issues and flag safety concerns before they become liability problems. Service requests from residents, handled with urgency and genuine follow-through. Unit turns on vacant apartments, preventative maintenance scheduling, janitorial support, and help managing inventory and supply levels across both properties. You'll document completed work accurately and communicate anything that needs escalation to the Service Manager or Property Manager at each site.

After-hours emergency coverage is part of the role. That's worth saying plainly. When something goes wrong at 11pm, this team needs people it can count on.

  • 1 to 2 years of maintenance experience, or equivalent hands-on training
  • EPA certification preferred
  • Solid working knowledge of appliance, electrical, and plumbing repair
  • Basic HVAC and electrical circuitry knowledge
  • Current on OSHA and building safety standards
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Own basic tools and know how to use them safely
  • Weekend availability required

What Van Metre Brings to the Table

Van Metre has been building and managing properties in the Washington, D.C. area since 1955. That history shows in how they structure their teams and invest in the people doing the hands-on work. Compensation for this role runs $21 to $23 per hour depending on experience, with an annual bonus potential of $5,000 paid out quarterly. There's also a meaningful benefits package: medical, dental, and vision coverage, a company-matched 401(k), generous paid time off (including your birthday and an annual physical day), tuition reimbursement, and a $900 annual wellness reimbursement. Company-paid certifications and a mentoring program mean there's a real path forward if you want to grow toward a Service Manager or lead technician role.

If you want one property, one routine, and minimal coordination overhead, this probably isn't the right fit. But if you thrive when you're trusted across multiple sites and you take real pride in the condition of the properties you touch, that's exactly the dynamic Van Metre is looking for here.

greenhouse_4240475009.title: FT Day Porter (Mon-Fri, 12PM - 9PM)
greenhouse_4240475009.rewritten_description:
Comstock's ParkX division keeps a portfolio of office properties running smoothly across the Arlington area, and the Day Porter role sits right at the center of that daily operation. This is a Monday through Friday position, 12PM to 9PM, so you'll be present through the full afternoon and evening cycle of tenant activity, including the wind-down hours when thorough cleaning and restocking actually gets done properly.

What You'll Actually Do

Your day covers the full range of commercial janitorial work: floors, restrooms, kitchens, meeting rooms, and common areas across an office environment. You'll empty trash and recycling, monitor supply levels, maintain your janitorial closet in organized and hazard-free condition, and complete end-of-shift documentation before handing off to the next shift. Beyond the cleaning checklist, you're also a visible presence for tenants and visitors. ParkX positions its porters as part of the property-facing team, so greeting people professionally and responding to cleanliness concerns quickly is genuinely part of the job, not an afterthought.

You'll report directly to a Senior Operations Manager and work within established schedules and checklists. When equipment needs attention or a safety issue comes up, you document it and flag it to management rather than letting it slide. Flexibility matters here: the role includes availability for after-hours and weekend coverage during events or peak periods.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Comfort working independently with minimal supervision once trained
  • Physical ability to stand for extended periods, lift up to 50 pounds, and work in variable temperature and chemical exposure conditions
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to prioritize tasks when multiple things need attention at once
  • A professional, approachable manner with tenants, guests, and coworkers
  • Willingness to cover for colleagues and flex into weekend or event shifts when needed

Context Worth Knowing

Arlington's office market has seen significant flux over the past few years, with mixed-use and transit-oriented properties holding up better than traditional suburban office stock. Comstock's ParkX properties tend to sit in that better-positioned category, which means consistent occupancy and tenant expectations that run high. A porter who treats tenant-facing interactions with the same care as the cleaning work itself will stand out here. The 12PM to 9PM shift is a real advantage for candidates who prefer afternoon hours, and the free parking and EV charging benefit is genuinely useful given the cost of commuting in Northern Virginia.

greenhouse_4244480009.title: Property Manager (Altitude 970)
greenhouse_4244480009.rewritten_description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Property management at the site level is fundamentally a numbers discipline wrapped in a people job. The Property Manager at Altitude 970 in Kansas City needs to hold both at once. On any given morning, that might mean reviewing delinquency before 9am, walking a turn unit with maintenance to tighten up a punch list, then sitting down with a leasing consultant to talk traffic conversion. The financial acumen matters as much as the interpersonal range.

BAM Companies is looking for someone with at least five years of residential management experience, Class B or better preferred. That ceiling matters: Class B and above typically means tighter operational standards, more resident expectation management, and less tolerance for deferred maintenance creeping into your NOI. If you've managed a property where every line item in the budget had a story, you'll fit the financial discipline this role requires.

What You'll Own Day to Day

The core responsibilities here cover the full site P&L: budgeting, rent collection, cost control, and occupancy performance. You'll lead leasing, maintenance, and admin staff, which means your coaching instincts are just as important as your ability to read a T-12. Retention strategy, marketing execution, and resident relations all fall under your umbrella. Fair housing compliance and asset care round out the operational scope.

Strong candidates in this type of role usually separate themselves on two fronts: financial ownership and team development. A lot of managers can execute tasks. Fewer can look at a month-end variance report, diagnose why NOI slipped, and then build a plan that the team actually executes. Fewer still can develop a leasing consultant into someone who closes consistently and handles difficult conversations without escalating everything upward. Both skills matter here.

  • 5+ years of residential property management experience, Class B or higher preferred
  • Demonstrated team leadership, including leasing and maintenance staff
  • Hands-on experience with budgeting, rent collection, and cost control
  • Proficiency with property management software and CRM systems
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Working knowledge of fair housing regulations

What's Distinctive About BAM

BAM Companies positions itself as a leadership development organization, not just an operator. For a Property Manager, that framing is meaningful. It suggests the company invests in the people running its sites rather than treating the PM seat as a steady-state role. The pay range for this position sits between $65,000 and $75,000, determined by experience, education, and overall compensation context. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, disability, pet insurance, life insurance, a housing discount at BAM properties, and a front-loaded PTO structure that gives you 88 hours at 90 days with more added at your one-year mark.

Kansas City's multifamily market has stayed relatively stable compared to the oversupply corrections hitting Sun Belt metros, which means a skilled PM here is managing for performance rather than just survival. Occupancy pressure is real but manageable, and a disciplined operator who keeps delinquency tight and retention strong can show genuinely clean numbers on a T-12. greenhouse_4243883009.title: Sales & Resident Experience Consultant - 176
greenhouse_4243883009.rewritten_description:
Leasing consultant roles at owner-operated multifamily companies tend to be more dynamic than their counterparts at third-party management firms. When the company owns the asset, the leasing function ties directly to NOI, and your closing performance shows up in the numbers everyone watches. At Thurman Lofts, Berkshire Residential is looking for someone who understands that distinction.

What This Role Actually Involves

The day-to-day here centers on converting traffic into signed leases. Berkshire sets a clear benchmark of at least a 20% closing ratio, which means you'll need to track your own numbers and hold yourself accountable to them. You'll manage the full leasing cycle: greeting prospects, touring units, following up, and guiding people through the decision to call this place home. Tour routes and model units are your responsibility to inspect and maintain, because presentation directly affects conversion.

Beyond traffic and tours, you'll keep a working knowledge of local market conditions, including what competitors are offering in terms of concessions and pricing, so you can position the property accurately. You'll also handle resident communications and contribute ideas to the property manager on marketing and resident satisfaction initiatives. Administrative accuracy matters here: lease files, guest cards, and follow-up logs need to be kept with real attention to detail.

What the Role Requires vs. What It Builds

Coming in, Berkshire expects at least two years of customer-facing experience, comfort with technology platforms, and strong written and verbal communication skills. These aren't negotiable because the pace of a leasing office doesn't leave room for a long ramp-up on the basics.

What this role builds is different. Consultants who pay attention to market conditions and closing patterns develop a genuine understanding of how occupancy decisions get made at the property level. You'll start to see the connection between your individual closing ratio and the community's overall occupancy, which is exactly the kind of thinking that prepares someone to step into an assistant manager or leasing manager position. Berkshire's in-house ownership structure also means you're working within a single portfolio culture rather than rotating between ownership groups, so institutional knowledge compounds over time.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The candidates who do well in roles like this aren't just personable. They're also self-directed. A leasing consultant who needs a manager to set their daily priorities tends to struggle; one who tracks their own traffic-to-lease conversion and adjusts their approach accordingly tends to thrive. Berkshire's culture emphasizes entrepreneurial ownership at every level, so people who show up waiting to be told what to do won't find the same fit as those who treat the property like their own small business.

  • At least two years of transferable customer service experience
  • Comfort adapting to leasing software and other property technology
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
  • Ability to maintain a professional, welcoming leasing environment
  • Attention to detail in administrative tasks and resident records

The position is based in California with a pay range of $21.50 to $25.00 per hour, depending on experience. Benefits include retirement, health coverage, paid time off including parental leave, and a 25% rent discount. Bonuses are also part of the package.

greenhouse_5213631008.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_5213631008.rewritten_description:
Leasing is a people skill first. The ability to read a prospect's hesitation, pivot your pitch without making it feel like a pitch, and turn a casual tour into a signed lease, that's the core of what this role demands. Bozzuto is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their Clermont, FL community, and the skills that will carry you here are relational, communicative, and genuinely sales-minded in equal measure.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

You'll spend a meaningful portion of your time converting inbound and outbound leads into scheduled tours, which means your written and verbal communication has to be sharp, warm, and persuasive without feeling scripted. Follow-up is where most leasing consultants either win or lose deals. Bozzuto expects you to stay on top of prospects with helpful, specific information about the community and the surrounding area, not just generic replies.

Touring skills matter just as much. A good tour isn't a walkthrough; it's a conversation where you listen for what the prospect actually values and connect it back to what the community offers. That takes curiosity and presence, not just a memorized script about square footage.

Social media is a genuine part of this job, not an afterthought. You'll create and post content on platforms like Facebook and Instagram to build community awareness and keep interest alive. Candidates who treat this as a creative outlet, rather than a chore, tend to do better here.

One honest note on schedule: this role requires working three weekends per month, with two weekday days off in exchange. Weekends are when most prospects are out looking, so it's where leasing happens. If your lifestyle can accommodate that rhythm, it works. If weekends are a hard limit, this role probably isn't the right fit.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A typical day might start with reviewing new leads from overnight inquiries, sending personalized follow-ups, and confirming afternoon tours. Midday, you're walking prospects through the community, answering questions about lease terms, amenities, and the neighborhood. Clermont sits in Lake County, west of Orlando, with a growing residential base and strong demand from families and remote workers relocating from larger metros. Knowing the local area, nearby shopping, commute patterns, proximity to I-4 and the Turnpike, is a real advantage when talking to prospects who are still figuring out if Clermont is the right fit for them.

Between tours, you might be posting an Instagram story, updating your CRM notes, or following up with someone who toured last week and hasn't decided yet.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Bozzuto operates at a level where culture and resident experience are central to the brand, not just talking points. The consultants who thrive tend to genuinely care about the people moving in, not just closing the lease. That care shows up in the little things: remembering a prospect's dog's name, knowing which floor plan works for a home office, flagging a maintenance issue before a new resident notices it.

  • Customer-focused mindset with real follow-through
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with social media content creation
  • Sales instincts paired with genuine warmth
  • Proficiency with software, apps, and property management platforms
  • Professional presentation and attention to detail

Compensation sits between $47,000 and $50,000 annually, with bonus opportunities on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement. For someone early in a property management career, this role builds a strong foundation. Leasing consultants who develop both their sales numbers and their resident relationship skills often move into assistant manager or leasing manager positions within a few years.

greenhouse_7908084.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
greenhouse_7908084.rewritten_description:
Weinstein Properties runs a straightforward operation: they own and manage their communities directly, which means the person giving you direction is the same person accountable for the property's condition. There's no third-party management layer, no conflicting priorities from an outside owner. Standards stay consistent, and when leadership says they support the team, it actually shows up in how the day-to-day works.

What You'll Actually Do

The bulk of your time goes to work orders in occupied units. Residents call in issues, you troubleshoot them, you fix them. HVAC is a big part of that, which is why the EPA certification matters here, not as a checkbox but as something you'll use regularly. Plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry: all of it comes through the queue. You'll also help with turns and make-readies when units come vacant, which means punch lists, coordinating with the team, and getting units rent-ready on schedule. Pool areas, grounds, and amenities are part of the picture too.

The on-call rotation is real. You'll share it with the team, but you should go in knowing that after-hours calls happen. The $150 weekly on-call pay applies whether your phone rings or not, and there's an additional $150 for holiday on-call coverage. That's a straightforward acknowledgment from the company that being available has a cost, and they're compensating for it.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of hands-on apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required, not preferred)
  • Demonstrated HVAC troubleshooting and repair ability
  • Comfort working independently and coordinating within a team
  • Reliable transportation and a valid driver's license
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and work both indoors and outdoors year-round
  • Proficiency with basic computer tools: work order systems, Outlook, mobile devices
  • Ability to climb ladders and stairs, and operate a golf cart on property

Strong candidates here aren't just technically capable. They communicate well with residents, they close their work orders with care, and they treat occupied units with respect. A tech who can fix the HVAC but leaves a mess or keeps residents in the dark doesn't last long in a community that cares about its reputation.

The Role in Context

Fort Worth's residential market has stayed active, and well-maintained communities in the north corridor hold their occupancy because residents notice when maintenance is sharp. This position pays $20 per hour to start, with room to move up based on experience. There's a quarterly bonus of up to $980 tied to property and team performance, a rent discount, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, and full medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus a 401(k) with company match.

For a tech with solid HVAC skills and a few years of apartment experience, this kind of in-house ownership structure tends to offer more stability and clearer advancement than a scattered portfolio managed by a third party. Weinstein notes that internal growth is real here, and for someone who eventually wants to move into a lead tech or maintenance supervisor role, that path is easier to walk when the company already knows your work.

greenhouse_7728366003.title: Maintenance Supervisor (Oak & Umber)
greenhouse_7728366003.rewritten_description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance supervision at scale demands a specific combination of technical depth, crew leadership, and budget discipline. At Prometheus Real Estate Group's Oak and Umber community in Sunnyvale, those three skill sets run together daily. This isn't a role where you hand off work orders and check boxes. You're running physical operations for a property that's part of a 13,000-unit privately held portfolio, one that Prometheus has built and managed in-house since 1965. That vertical integration matters: acquisitions, development, value-add renovations, and operations all sit under one roof, which means the maintenance team is close to capex decisions and renovation scopes in ways that don't happen at third-party management shops.

The technical baseline here is real. Five or more years in apartment maintenance, at least two in a supervisory seat, and a minimum of three certifications from programs like BOMA, IREM, or vocational trades. You'll need working fluency in federal, state, and local safety regulations, because compliance in California's regulatory environment is not an area where approximation works. The ability to read operating manuals, interpret safety rules, and translate both into team behavior is a daily requirement, not an occasional one.

What Running This Neighborhood Actually Looks Like

Your day moves between the budget and the building. On the cost side, you're managing vendor and contractor relationships with an eye on spend, keeping maintenance functions cost-effective without deferring work that creates larger problems downstream. On the physical side, you're overseeing ongoing safety training, capital projects, and inventory management while also being the person your team calls when something goes sideways after hours. On-call isn't a footnote here. It's a real part of the job, and Prometheus pays standby and on-call premium pay to reflect that.

The leadership piece is equally concrete. You'll hire and train your maintenance staff, mentor them through technical challenges, and resolve the interpersonal friction that comes with any crew operating under pressure. The community's residents (Prometheus calls them Neighbors) expect fast, quality responses. Your team's consistency is what makes that possible.

  • Minimum 5 years apartment maintenance experience, 2 years supervisory
  • At least 3 certifications from recognized maintenance or trades programs (BOMA, IREM, vocational)
  • Solid knowledge of California safety regulations and the ability to apply them operationally
  • Able to lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally; role is physically active
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Available for on-call response as needed

What Makes Prometheus a Different Operator

Prometheus holds its properties long-term and reinvests in them. For a Maintenance Supervisor, that distinction has real operational consequences: capital projects get funded, standards don't erode to protect short-term NOI, and the team you build is meant to stay. Strong candidates for this role aren't just technically sharp. They think about maintenance as an asset preservation function. If you've supervised a team through a renovation cycle or a lease-up and kept physical operations steady while the property was in flux, that experience translates directly here.

greenhouse_4244033009.title: Maintenance Supervisor
greenhouse_4244033009.location: Yester Oaks - 100 Yester Oaks Way East - Greensboro, NC - 27455
greenhouse_4244033009.rewritten_description:
Yester Oaks is a residential community where the maintenance supervisor sets the tone for how residents experience their home every single day. Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring for that role now, and it's worth understanding what the position actually demands before you apply.

This isn't a solo technician role. You'll lead a maintenance team, coordinate vendor work, manage the unit turn process, and keep a preventative maintenance calendar running across the full property. Budget awareness matters here too: you'll monitor spending, track inventory, and pull in bids when capital work comes up. The make-ready side of the job is yours to own, from scheduling turns to walking vacant units yourself before a new resident gets their keys. If a punch list item slips through, it's on your watch.

On any given weekday, you might start the morning reviewing open work orders and assigning them across your team, check in with a vendor finishing up a scope from last week, walk a turned unit to confirm it's truly move-in ready, and spend part of the afternoon troubleshooting an HVAC issue that came in overnight. The afternoon might end with a quick team huddle or a call with the office about an upcoming lease-up push. The hours are Monday through Friday, 8 to 5, but there's an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That part is real, and it's worth factoring into your decision.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is the combination of hands-on technical skill and genuine patience with people. Supervisors who only fix things well but struggle to mentor or communicate tend to create friction on the team and with residents. Hawthorne's culture leans into connection and accountability together, so someone who leads by example and doesn't disappear when things get hard will thrive here. Prior lead technician or supervisory experience is a real differentiator, not just a checkbox.

What You'll Need

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least 3 years of apartment maintenance or skilled trade experience (HVAC, plumbing, or electrical)
  • Prior supervisory or lead technician experience, strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA certification (required)
  • CPO certification (preferred, and required in some states)

Compensation includes hourly pay plus a monthly renewal bonus, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also offers an internal career path program and education reimbursement specifically for maintenance skills development, which is a meaningful perk for someone who wants to keep growing in the trade.

If you're the kind of person who takes quiet pride in a well-run property and wants a team that will actually invest in your career, this role at Yester Oaks is worth a close look.

greenhouse_4240502009.title: Limpiador Residencial
greenhouse_4240502009.rewritten_description:
Comstock's residential porter role at their Ashburn, VA property is the kind of position where your presence is felt the moment someone walks through the front door. The cleanliness and condition of common areas shape how residents and visitors feel about where they live or work, and that's the direct result of this person's daily effort.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're responsible for keeping lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and shared spaces clean and presentable across assigned areas. That means following scheduled checklists, responding to cleaning concerns as they come up, and completing pressure washing assignments in the areas management designates. You'll also support event setup and breakdown when the property hosts gatherings, which adds some variety to the routine but also means weekend and occasional off-hours availability is part of the deal.

You'll maintain your supply closet and storage areas in good order, track cleaning inventory, and handle chemicals according to safety standards. At the end of each shift, you'll complete required documentation and hand off properly to the next person. If a teammate is out, you may be asked to cover. The work is physical: you'll be on your feet for extended stretches, lifting up to 50 pounds, working in varying temperatures indoors and out, and sometimes in conditions that include dust, fumes, or cleaning agents.

One thing that sets this role apart from a standard janitorial position is the guest interaction piece. You're wearing a ParkX Porter uniform, arriving before your shift starts, and greeting residents and visitors as part of the job. That's not incidental. Comstock expects the person in this role to carry themselves with a service mindset, not just a cleaning mindset.

Who Tends to Do Well Here

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Flexibility to work weekends and during events or high-activity periods
  • Strong reliability and personal accountability
  • Comfortable working independently with minimal supervision
  • Able to manage multiple tasks and prioritize in a busy environment
  • A genuine ease with people from different backgrounds

The candidates who stand out aren't necessarily the ones with the longest cleaning resume. They're the ones who show up on time every shift, notice things before they become problems, and treat every resident interaction as part of the job rather than an interruption to it. Self-direction matters here because you won't always have someone looking over your shoulder.

Benefits and Growth

Comstock offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, and life insurance. There's annual funding for professional development, a parental leave program, and free parking with EV charging on site. The company also notes that this role sits within a growing portfolio, which means advancement opportunities exist for people who prove themselves.

For someone who wants a foothold in property operations, this kind of role builds real familiarity with how a residential property runs. Porters who develop strong relationships with maintenance and management teams often move into maintenance tech or lead porter positions over time.

greenhouse_5216506008.title: Evening Concierge
greenhouse_5216506008.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is the Monday through Friday, 3PM to 11PM shift, which means you're covering the hours when the building truly comes alive. Residents are returning from work, packages are stacking up at the front desk, guests are arriving, and the common spaces are in active use. You're the consistent face during all of it. You handle front desk operations, manage package room organization, coordinate club room and freight elevator reservations, and field whatever residents need as the evening unfolds. You also plan and execute resident events that build genuine community, not just a sign-in sheet and some appetizers.

Bozzuto puts real weight on the concierge role as a driver of resident satisfaction and retention. That means you're expected to know residents by name, learn their preferences, and personalize every interaction. You'll also help generate positive online visibility by encouraging happy residents to share their experiences on social platforms, and you'll contribute to the community's social media presence yourself.

What You Bring

  • At least two years working in hospitality, retail, hotel, or a similar customer-facing environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to handle sensitive situations with composure
  • Comfort with software, apps, and property management tools used at the front desk
  • A sharp, professional presentation that reflects the quality of the community
  • Physical ability to lift up to 25 pounds, which becomes relevant quickly during peak delivery seasons
  • Genuine attentiveness to detail, especially in keeping logs, reservations, and front desk records accurate

Context Worth Knowing

Falls Church sits in one of the more competitive Class A rental submarkets in Northern Virginia. Properties in this corridor compete hard on resident experience, and concierge quality is a real differentiator. Bozzuto manages a significant share of upscale multifamily in the DC metro region, and their communities tend to attract residents with high service expectations. The evening shift in particular requires someone who can handle the pace of post-5PM traffic without losing the warmth and attentiveness that defines the role.

What separates strong candidates here from average ones isn't just friendliness. It's anticipation. The best concierges in this type of environment notice what a resident needs before being asked, remember small details from previous conversations, and treat every interaction as an opportunity to reinforce why someone chose to live there. That instinct, more than any specific credential, is what Bozzuto is hiring for in this role.

The salary range for this position is $48,000 to $51,500, with eligibility for additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

greenhouse_5216553008.title: Maintenance Technician
greenhouse_5216553008.rewritten_description:
Bozzuto operates a portfolio that spans design, construction, and third-party management, and the maintenance technician role sits right at the intersection of resident satisfaction and asset preservation. At a Bozzuto-managed property in Fairfax, that means your work shows up directly in renewal rates, online ratings, and ultimately NOI. A slow turn or a recurring HVAC ticket left unresolved doesn't just frustrate a resident. It costs the property.

The day-to-day here covers the full range of building maintenance: service ticket resolution across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair; make-ready work to get vacant units back on the market; and general upkeep that keeps the community presentable and safe. Snow removal and grounds work come with the territory. So does an on-call rotation, which means some evenings and weekends are part of the deal. That's the honest reality of maintenance work at any residential property, and it's worth knowing upfront.

Bozzuto is looking for someone with beginner to intermediate skills across the core trades. You don't need to be an expert in every system, but you should be comfortable diagnosing a problem and knowing when to escalate. Strong candidates in this role tend to close tickets fast and clean, communicate clearly with residents during the process, and show up to on-call situations without needing to be tracked down. The technicians who advance here treat a punch list like a scorecard.

One concrete perk worth noting: after your first 12 months, Bozzuto covers the cost of your EPA 608 Universal Refrigerant Certification. For anyone building a career in HVAC and property maintenance, that certification opens doors. It's a real investment, not a line item buried in the benefits summary.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience or formal trade education in building maintenance
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance systems
  • Reliable personal transportation for commuting and on-call response
  • Physical ability to handle frequent lifting in the 25 to 50 pound range
  • Comfort with software and property management apps used for work orders
  • Clear communication skills and a professional presentation
  • Availability for on-call emergency coverage as part of a rotation

The salary range for this position runs from $50,000 to approximately $53,000 annually, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement for ongoing education.

greenhouse_4237969009.title: Centralized Painter - Colorado Springs, CO
greenhouse_4237969009.rewritten_description:
It's 8 a.m. and you're already loading your van with paint, primer, and patching compound before heading to the first property on your route. By noon, you've finished a full unit repaint and you're halfway through a touch-up on a second. This is centralized painter work: less standing around waiting for direction, more moving efficiently through a portfolio of properties with clear daily output expectations.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Cortland is hiring a centralized painter to support unit turns and ongoing upkeep across their Colorado Springs portfolio. The role is travel-based by design. You'll drive between assigned properties rather than staying planted at one community, which suits painters who like variety and work well without someone looking over their shoulder all day.

Day-to-day, the workload typically runs to one full unit repaint or two touch-ups per shift, depending on what the turn schedule demands. Beyond paint application itself, the role includes drywall repairs: patching, sanding, and texture matching. Exterior work comes up too, so you'll need comfort with ladders, lifts, and scaffolding and a working knowledge of elevated-work safety procedures and OSHA requirements.

Spray equipment is a real part of this job, not an occasional add-on. You'll be expected to mix and match coatings, maintain your sprayer, and follow proper maintenance protocols. The paint shop at each location needs to stay clean, stocked, and organized. That's on you too.

You'll log completed work, materials used, and any follow-up items in a CMMS platform. If you haven't used maintenance management software before, there's room to learn, but you should be comfortable picking up new tools quickly.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least two years of interior residential painting experience; custom home background is a plus
  • Solid brush, roller, and spray application skills with strong spray-prep technique
  • Ability to perform small drywall repairs and match texture (larger repairs are a bonus)
  • Valid driver's license, required vehicle insurance, and comfort with regular travel between sites
  • Familiarity with OSHA regulations and MSDS requirements
  • Ability to work at heights and on weekends when the turn schedule calls for it
  • Clear written and verbal communication in English

The pay range for this role is $24 to $26 per hour.

One honest note about this kind of role: the daily output expectations are real. One full repaint per day is a solid pace, and staying on schedule matters because maintenance teams and leasing staff are counting on clean, ready units. Painters who thrive here tend to be the ones who take personal ownership of their work quality and don't need a supervisor to tell them when something isn't finished right. If you've built a reputation for consistent, clean work in residential settings, this kind of centralized structure tends to reward that.

greenhouse_4240610009.title: Front Door Waste Technician,  Part Time - Cortland Luxe Shadow Creek
greenhouse_4240610009.rewritten_description:
It's 8 p.m. on a Tuesday, and residents along your assigned route have set their bags outside. You move efficiently from door to door, hamper in tow, keeping the hallways clear and the property looking exactly the way a Cortland community is supposed to look.

This part-time Front Door Waste Technician role at Cortland Luxe Shadow Creek in Houston supports the daily valet trash program for a multifamily apartment community. It's physical, outdoor, route-based work that runs on a consistent schedule. You'll collect resident waste bags, transport them to onsite compactors or containers, and keep common areas clean throughout the property, including pool areas, dog waste stations, mail kiosks, parking lots, and stairwells.

What the Work Actually Involves

Beyond the route itself, you'll monitor for improperly disposed or prohibited waste and take appropriate action when you find it. Spills around doorsteps, sidewalks, and compactor areas get cleaned up as part of your standard responsibilities. You'll operate compactors safely when needed and keep the surrounding areas clear of debris and obstructions.

Every shift, you'll log start and end times and complete required reporting through a mobile app, including photos. This documentation matters. It creates accountability and helps the onsite team stay informed. You'll interact with residents, staff, and management along the way, so your manner in those moments reflects directly on the community's reputation. Cortland communities are positioned as premium living environments, and the cleanliness of common areas is part of what residents are paying for.

What You Bring

  • A high school diploma or equivalent (preferred)
  • At least one year in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA regulations related to waste handling
  • Strong communication skills; bilingual ability is a plus
  • Physical ability to climb stairs, walk long distances, and lift up to 50 lbs
  • Comfort working outdoors in Houston's heat, humidity, and occasional rain
  • A valid Class E driver's license for local driving as needed
  • A personal smartphone (Android 2.2+ or iPhone iOS 4.3+) with data and active email for shift documentation

One thing that separates reliable candidates in this role: consistency. Routes don't get done halfway. Residents notice immediately when a bag gets missed or an area looks neglected. The people who thrive here take the work seriously even when no one is watching, show up on time, and communicate clearly if something is off on the property. That dependability is genuinely valued on a multifamily operations team.

greenhouse_5993732004.title: Compliance Specialist
greenhouse_5993732004.rewritten_description:
Affordable Housing compliance work sits at the intersection of regulatory precision and resident impact. Every file you review carries real consequences: a missed eligibility issue can jeopardize a property's tax credit status, while an unnecessary denial can block a household from housing they qualify for. This role at Asset Living demands both kinds of accuracy.

The Skills This Role Draws On Immediately

You'll use file review and regulatory interpretation from day one. The core of the position is evaluating Affordable Housing resident applications against current LIHTC requirements, confirming eligibility, and completing that review within a 24-hour window. That turnaround standard requires you to work with speed and accuracy simultaneously, not sequentially. Proficiency with RealPage OneSite Tax Credit is specifically relevant here, so familiarity with that platform shortens your ramp time considerably.

Strong written communication matters more in this role than people often expect. Your file reviews create a documented record that outside entities examine during tax credit audits. Vague notes or incomplete documentation can create compliance exposure even when the underlying decision was correct. Clear, precise written work protects the property and the portfolio.

What This Role Builds Over Time

The requirement to earn the Housing Credit Certified Professional (HCCP) designation within your first two years is a built-in investment in your professional standing. HCCP is a nationally recognized credential, and holding it opens doors to senior compliance roles, portfolio-level oversight positions, and consulting work within the affordable housing sector. You'll also attend TDHCA trainings annually and participate in third-party tax credit reviews, which means you build direct familiarity with how regulatory agencies and outside auditors evaluate compliance programs. That exposure is hard to replicate outside of a role like this one.

Monitoring shifts in LIHTC regulations and translating those changes into updated procedures is another skill this role develops deliberately. Tax credit rules do change, and the compliance specialist who can track those changes, interpret their practical effect, and implement modifications at the property level becomes genuinely valuable to a third-party management firm operating across a large affordable housing portfolio.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

  • Comfort with a 50% travel requirement, including property visits, trainings, and conferences
  • A working knowledge of HUD programs, even if LIHTC is your primary focus
  • The organizational discipline to manage multiple file reviews under tight turnaround windows without cutting corners on documentation
  • Genuine interest in earning and maintaining the HCCP credential, not just completing it as a checkbox

Asset Living operates as a fee management firm across multifamily, single-family rental, build-to-rent, student housing, and affordable housing divisions. That breadth means a compliance specialist here works within a large, structured operation with real infrastructure behind it, including training resources, established procedures, and a compliance team with institutional knowledge. If you're building a career in affordable housing compliance, that organizational depth matters.

greenhouse_5993455004.title: Operations Specialist
greenhouse_5993455004.rewritten_description:
Operations roles at third-party management firms tend to sit at the intersection of everything: financial reporting, client communication, internal coordination, and the occasional moment where you're fielding a frustrated resident call while simultaneously pulling rent comps for a regional VP. That's the honest picture of what this role looks like at Asset Living, one of the larger fee management operators in multifamily, single-family rental, and student housing.

What This Role Actually Covers

The Operations Specialist supports senior-level portfolio managers across a range of tasks that don't fit neatly into one department. On any given week, you might be reviewing historical income and expense data for a Class B garden-style property, preparing a quarterly performance report for an owner, gathering rent comparable data from third-party sources, and coordinating travel logistics for a regional manager heading out for property visits. You'll also field resident calls that come in at the corporate level, which means you need to be calm, clear, and professional even when the person on the other end isn't.

The financial side of this role carries real weight. Collecting and reviewing T-12 data, understanding what drives NOI movement across a portfolio, and presenting that information clearly to clients requires both accuracy and the ability to translate numbers into plain language. Errors here don't just get flagged internally; they affect owner relationships.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • Strong Excel skills, not just functional ones. You should be comfortable building and auditing reports, not just filling in templates.
  • Familiarity with property management software like MRI or One-Site is a genuine advantage, though not required.
  • A background or coursework in finance, real estate, or economics helps you interpret what the numbers are actually saying.
  • You manage competing deadlines without losing track of details. Multiple senior managers may be pulling your time simultaneously.
  • You communicate professionally with clients and residents alike, adjusting your tone and level of detail for the audience.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this kind of support role is the ability to work ahead of requests. Senior managers shouldn't have to follow up twice. If you read a report and notice something looks off before sending it, if you confirm travel details proactively rather than waiting to be asked, that instinct is what makes this role genuinely valuable rather than just functional.

Context and Growth

Asset Living operates across multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, and active adult communities, which means the portfolio you're supporting isn't uniform. You'll develop fluency across asset types and management structures that most property management roles don't offer this early. Operations Specialists who perform well here often move into analyst, regional coordinator, or asset management support roles as the company grows. This role is a real on-ramp to the analytical and operational side of third-party management, not just an administrative holding pattern.

The position is based in Bentonville, AR, with travel estimated at roughly 10% annually for property visits and internal meetings.

greenhouse_7725242003.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - Avion
greenhouse_7725242003.rewritten_description:
Three years of hands-on residential maintenance experience, EPA/HVAC certification, and the organizational discipline to keep a team on schedule. Those are the core skills this role runs on. If you've got all three and you're comfortable owning the maintenance operation at a multifamily community, this is worth a closer look.

What This Role Actually Requires

The Lead Maintenance Technician at Avion in Bozeman is effectively a working supervisor. You're not just fixing things. You're scheduling your team's daily workloads, managing turns, coordinating contractors, and keeping inventory stocked and organized. You'll run regular property inspections, track service requests through software, and handle preventative maintenance across HVAC systems, irrigation, appliances, pools, and building structures. The job is Monday through Friday, 9 to 5, with on-call rotation. Full-time, not seasonal.

You'll work closely with the Business Manager and leasing office to make sure make-ready units are show-ready and vacant homes are genuinely move-in ready. That coordination piece matters more than people expect. A unit that's technically fixed but not punch-listed properly creates friction with the leasing side fast.

You're also responsible for hiring and developing the service team beneath you, which means you need some comfort with people management, not just wrenches. Compliance with state, federal, and local regulations is part of the job too. That's not a footnote.

Skills This Role Sharpens

The supervisory layer here is real. Technicians who step into lead roles often underestimate how much of the job shifts from doing to planning and directing. Scheduling forecasted workloads, managing contractor relationships, and keeping the shop organized while also staying current on service requests builds a skill set that transfers directly into Maintenance Director or Service Manager roles. Bozeman's growth as a market means multifamily here isn't slowing down, and experienced leads who know how to run a tight operation are genuinely hard to find in mountain-west markets.

What Olympus Brings to the Role

Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer from the National Apartment Association three consecutive years. That's not nothing. Their benefits package is comprehensive: medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, sabbatical, and both short and long-term disability coverage. The pay range comes in at $30 to $35 per hour depending on experience and location, with monthly and quarterly bonuses available.

They leave the shop cleaner than they found it. That's the profile that tends to succeed in a lead role at a company that's clearly paying attention to culture and accountability.

greenhouse_7915007.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_7915007.rewritten_description:
It's 9:15 on a Saturday morning. A prospective resident just walked in without an appointment, a current resident is waiting at the desk about a billing question, and you have two leasing applications to process before noon. That's a normal morning at Bexley at Anderson Mill.

Weinstein Properties is a family-owned company that has operated apartment communities for over 70 years, with a portfolio of more than 60 properties across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. The Cedar Park location is looking for an Assistant Property Manager who can hold their own in a full-contact leasing office environment. Starting pay is $23 per hour, with increases based on experience and quarterly bonuses built into the compensation structure. Rotating Saturdays are part of the schedule.

The Day-to-Day Work

This role covers a wide range of operational tasks, and that range is real, not just recruiting language. On any given day you might be responding to internet leads, scheduling tours, walking a made-ready apartment to confirm it's punch-list clean, posting rent payments, and following up on delinquent balances. You'll process leasing applications, prepare lease paperwork, collect security deposits, and get signatures. When residents have questions about renewals, notices to vacate, transfers, or pet addendums, you're one of the first points of contact. You'll coordinate with maintenance on work orders, follow up with residents on open requests, and help process move-out security deposit dispositions. Resident events are also part of the job, including planning and hosting. You'll support the Property Manager and, at times, help train and guide others on the team.

Prior property management experience is a plus, but Weinstein will train the right person who comes from a customer service, sales, or hospitality background. The expectation is that you learn fast and stay organized while the work keeps moving around you.

What This Role Actually Requires

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to handle difficult conversations calmly
  • Comfort working in a physically active role: expect time on your feet, walking the property, and inspecting units
  • Attention to detail when handling lease documents, applications, and financial transactions
  • Ability to shift priorities mid-task without losing accuracy
  • Availability for rotating Saturdays and occasional extended hours for resident events or weather-related situations
  • Goal-oriented approach and willingness to pitch in outside your formal job description when the team needs it

One honest note on this role: the combination of leasing, resident services, administrative work, and maintenance coordination means the job rarely lets you settle into one task for long. If you thrive when the day goes sideways, that's a genuine advantage here. If you need a predictable routine to do your best work, this probably isn't the right fit.

Weinstein has a track record of promoting from within. Many people in leadership roles at the company started in leasing or assistant manager positions. The skills you build here, including delinquency follow-up, make-ready coordination, and lease administration, transfer directly to a Property Manager role or broader multi-site responsibilities down the road.

Weinstein Properties is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
