greenhouse_6000380004.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work at a residential community is rarely glamorous, but it's genuinely important. When a resident's heat goes out at midnight or a work order backlog piles up after a holiday weekend, the maintenance technician is the person who holds the property together. Cottonwood Residential is filling that role at Cason Estates Apartments in Murfreesboro, TN, and they're looking for someone who takes the craft seriously.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you'll move through a mix of scheduled work orders and reactive repairs across the community. Plumbing issues, electrical troubleshooting, carpentry, appliance repairs, grounds-related fixes , the variety keeps things interesting, but it also means you need a genuine base of hands-on skills rather than depth in just one trade. HVAC troubleshooting is a particular area of emphasis here, so comfort diagnosing heating and cooling problems will serve you well. If you carry an EPA Type II or Universal certification, or a CPO, bring that with you. If not, those credentials are worth pursuing as you grow in the role.

You'll also share on-call rotation for after-hours emergency calls. That's worth naming plainly: evenings and weekends are part of the job, and urgent situations don't wait for business hours. The Service Manager provides support during those calls, so you're not working without backup, but you do need to be the kind of person who can respond calmly under pressure and represent the community well even at odd hours.

The physical demands are real. You'll be on your feet most of the day, lifting up to 50 lbs, climbing ladders, working in tight spaces, and covering ground across the property. A valid driver's license is required.

Who Fits This Role Well

The candidates who thrive here tend to share a few traits beyond technical ability. They communicate clearly with residents , not just fixing the problem, but leaving the interaction feeling professional and considerate. They manage their own time across a work order queue without constant hand-holding. And they treat the property with the same care they'd give their own home.

  • Solid troubleshooting skills across plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry
  • HVAC experience, especially diagnostics and repair
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (preferred, not required)
  • CPO certification (a plus)
  • Valid driver's license
  • Comfort working evenings, weekends, and on-call rotations
  • Ability to read safety and operating manuals and complete company documentation in English

Cottonwood offers health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits with coverage available quickly after hire, a 401k and HSA with company match, 10.5 paid holidays, and three weeks of paid time off eligible in the first year. For a maintenance role, that's a competitive package worth weighing seriously.

One honest note for anyone considering this path: maintenance technician roles at well-run communities are one of the cleaner routes into a Service Manager or Maintenance Supervisor position. You build a portfolio of completed work, develop vendor relationships, and learn how a property operates from the ground up. That experience transfers directly if you want to move up within Cottonwood or across the industry later on.

greenhouse_4252609009.title: Leasing Consultant (Hayden Flats)
greenhouse_4252609009.rewritten_description:
Leasing is a contact sport. Every lead that comes in , by phone, email, or walk-in , is a chance to move occupancy and earn a commission. At Hayden Flats, a BAM Companies property in Bloomington, IN, the Leasing Consultant role puts those skills front and center from day one.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Conversion is the job. You're taking traffic and turning it into signed leases. That means reading prospects quickly, matching them to the right unit, and guiding them through an application without losing momentum. Follow-up discipline matters as much as the tour itself. A lead that goes cold is occupancy left on the table.

Communication is the other half of it. You'll work across phone, email, and in-person touchpoints, and the ability to stay organized across all three without dropping a prospect is what separates a 90% occupancy performer from someone stuck at 80%. Basic CRM proficiency is expected. If you've worked retail, hospitality, or inside sales, that multi-channel communication habit transfers directly here.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You're the first person a prospective resident meets. You'll greet walk-ins, run apartment tours, explain pricing and unit features, and close on applications and deposits. Between tours, you're responding to leads, updating prospect records, keeping show units and tour paths presentation-ready, and supporting marketing outreach and community events. Your property manager sets the leasing goals; your job is hitting them.

Weekends are part of the rotation. That's when traffic is highest, and that's when leases get signed. A valid driver's license and reliable vehicle are required.

What BAM Brings to the Table

BAM pays commission on signed leases, so strong closers earn more. The base pay range runs $17 to $19 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. Benefits start with 15.5 paid holidays from day one, PTO after 90 days, and a full insurance package including medical, dental, vision, and pet coverage. Housing discounts at BAM properties are also available.

For the right candidate, this role is a real entry point into property management. Leasing Consultants who understand traffic-to-lease ratios, resident experience, and the operational rhythm of a property tend to move into Assistant Manager roles where they own delinquency, reporting, and broader site performance. The skills you build here , closing, resident communication, data entry discipline , carry weight at every level of the business. A minimum of a high school diploma is required; some college is a plus, and NALP credentials or bilingual ability are preferred but not required.

greenhouse_4251165009.title: Leasing Consultant
greenhouse_4251165009.rewritten_description:
Lease-up and stabilized assets alike live or die by the quality of the leasing team. At a property like 20 Midtown, the Leasing Consultant role isn't just about showing units. It's about converting traffic into signed leases, building resident relationships that reduce turnover, and keeping the property's occupancy and delinquency picture healthy from the ground up.

Berkshire Residential Investments owns and manages its own portfolio, which means this is an in-house role with real operational stake in the outcome. You're not working for a third-party fee management shop where the asset is someone else's problem. Berkshire's people are, by their own account, what separates their properties from the competition, and that philosophy shapes how this team operates day to day.

What This Role Actually Involves

Your primary job is converting prospective residents into signed leases. Berkshire sets a floor of 20% closing ratio, which is a concrete benchmark worth noting. If you've worked leasing before, you know that number reflects consistent follow-up, a well-maintained tour route, and the ability to read what a prospect actually needs rather than just reciting floor plan specs.

Beyond closing, you'll keep the leasing office running professionally, maintain model and tour route presentation, track local market conditions and competitor activity, and communicate clearly with both prospects and current residents. Administrative accuracy matters here. Lease files, written communications, and follow-up documentation are part of the daily rhythm, not an afterthought.

You'll also contribute marketing ideas to the property manager, which means this role has some creative latitude if you've got opinions about what's working in the market and what isn't.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience, whether from property management or a transferable service background
  • Comfort with leasing software and the ability to pick up new platforms without hand-holding
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including professional resident correspondence
  • Genuine interest in helping people find a place to live, not just processing applications

What separates strong candidates from average ones at this level isn't usually hard knowledge. It's follow-through. Prospects who don't get a timely callback, tour routes that aren't checked before a showing, lease paperwork with errors. Those small gaps compound into occupancy problems. The consultants who build real closing ratios are the ones who treat every touchpoint as part of the sale, including the ones that happen after the tour ends.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, personal development planning, a 25% rent discount, and a benefits package. This role sits on a team that, if you're serious about a career in residential property management, can open doors toward leasing manager and eventually assistant property manager responsibilities as you build your track record.

greenhouse_5225125008.title: Groundskeeper - $1,500 Sign-On Bonus
greenhouse_5225125008.rewritten_description:
It's 7 a.m. on a Monday. Before most residents have poured their first cup of coffee, you're already moving through the property pulling trash, checking lights, and making sure the grounds look like someone actually cares. That's the job, and it matters more than people realize.

What the Role Involves

Bozzuto is hiring a Community Care Associate (Porter/Groundskeeper) at their Aberdeen, MD community, and they're offering a $1,500 sign-on bonus for the right person. This is a full-time, physical, get-your-hands-dirty position that keeps a multifamily community looking sharp and functioning properly day to day.

Daily responsibilities include trash pickup and cleaning trash areas, weed pulling, raking, and watering grounds, plus sweeping halls and curbs at least once a week. You'll check hall lights weekly, hose out hallways monthly, and power wash stairwells twice a year. The pool needs vacuuming, handrails need weekly attention, and bandit sign removal is a daily task. Snow removal gets added to the list seasonally. You'll also clean the clubhouse and common areas, deliver resident communications by 3 p.m. when needed, and support the maintenance team with tasks including painting as requested.

Reliable personal transportation to get to the property is required. Prior cleaning experience in multifamily or commercial settings is preferred. The role involves lifting up to 50 pounds and regular pushing, pulling, and climbing.

What Separates Good Candidates from Average Ones

Groundskeeping roles don't get enough credit for how much they affect a property's performance. Curb appeal drives traffic. A clean, well-maintained exterior signals to prospective residents that the whole operation is run well. The people who thrive in this role don't need to be told twice to handle something they noticed on their own. They're methodical about weekly and monthly tasks without letting the routine become invisible. If you've worked on a property before and you know the difference between a punch list item and a genuine maintenance issue worth flagging, that kind of awareness is genuinely useful here.

Bozzuto offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement. The salary range for the position is $42,024 to $43,000 annually, with additional bonus opportunities beyond the sign-on.

greenhouse_4252857009.title: Bilingual Screening & Applications Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
greenhouse_4252857009.rewritten_description:
Centralized leasing operations have changed how large multifamily portfolios convert traffic into signed leases. Instead of each community handling its own application queue, operators like Cortland route that work through a contact center where specialists own the process from submission to move-in. It keeps compliance tighter, applicant experience more consistent, and site teams focused on retention. This role sits at the center of that model.

What the Job Actually Involves

As a Bilingual Screening and Applications Specialist in Cortland's centralized contact center, you process rental applications, verify supporting documentation, and communicate with prospective residents across calls, emails, and chat, all at the same time. On any given shift you might be reviewing income verification for three applicants, updating statuses in OneSite or RealPage, and de-escalating a frustrated caller who hasn't heard back about their application in two days. The volume is real. The documentation requirements are precise. Fair Housing compliance isn't a checkbox here; it's a daily practice across every interaction.

Bilingual fluency is central to this role, not an add-on. A meaningful portion of applicants will communicate primarily in Spanish, and this position exists to make sure that experience doesn't degrade the moment language becomes a barrier. Strong candidates bring the same professionalism and clarity in both languages under volume pressure.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

  • Experience in a high-volume contact center, ideally in multifamily, where you've managed competing priorities without letting accuracy slip
  • Hands-on familiarity with platforms like Funnel, OneSite, or RealPage. You don't need to be re-trained on the basics
  • Demonstrated ability to handle confidential applicant information with discretion, income docs, ID verification, background results
  • Comfort working weekends and extended hours when leasing demand spikes
  • High school diploma or equivalent required; 2 or more years of customer service experience strongly preferred

The candidates who struggle in centralized leasing roles are usually strong communicators who underestimate the documentation side, or detail-oriented processors who lose the human element when volume climbs. This role needs both in equal measure. If you can hold a warm, clear conversation with an applicant in Spanish while simultaneously tracking where three other files stand in the pipeline, that's the skill set Cortland is looking for.

Cortland is a vertically integrated operator, ranked among the top 10 multifamily owners in the US, with in-house design, construction, and management under one roof. That structure means decisions move faster and the tools you work with are built for how the portfolio actually operates.

greenhouse_4252862009.title: Bilingual Screening & Applications Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
greenhouse_4252862009.rewritten_description:
A prospective resident calls in frustrated, three days into the application process, asking why their documentation hasn't been verified yet. You pull up their file, spot the missing item, explain exactly what's needed and why, and by the end of the call they feel guided rather than processed. That moment is the core of this role.

What This Role Actually Involves

Cortland, one of the country's top multifamily owners and operators, runs a centralized Contact Center that handles application processing across its portfolio. As a Bilingual Screening and Applications Specialist based in Sandy Springs, you'll own the stretch of the leasing journey between application submission and move-in. That means reviewing and processing rental applications for accuracy and compliance, collecting and verifying supporting documentation, and keeping applicants informed at every step through calls, emails, and chat. You'll handle multiple applicants simultaneously, which requires sharp prioritization and the kind of organized communication that prevents things from falling through the cracks. De-escalation is part of the work. Fair Housing compliance is non-negotiable. The bilingual requirement reflects Cortland's commitment to serving a diverse resident base, so fluency in both English and Spanish is essential to the position.

The tech stack includes platforms like Funnel, OneSite, and RealPage alongside CRM tools, and you'll need to move between systems efficiently in a high-volume environment. Weekends and extended hours come with the territory during peak leasing periods.

What Makes Someone Strong in This Role

The qualifications Cortland is looking for include:

  • At least two years of customer service experience, preferably in a contact center or multifamily housing environment
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Demonstrated comfort handling confidential applicant information with discretion
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and familiarity with property management software (Funnel, OneSite, RealPage)
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accuracy under pressure
  • Bilingual fluency in English and Spanish

The candidates who thrive here aren't just fast workers. They're people who understand that an application denial delivered without empathy can damage a brand, and that a well-handled difficult call can turn a frustrated prospect into a future resident. Experience inside a multifamily leasing office or centralized operations team carries real weight because the vocabulary, the compliance context, and the documentation expectations are already familiar.

From a career development angle, this role builds a skill set that translates directly into leasing management, compliance coordination, or regional operations support. Centralized contact center experience at a vertically integrated operator like Cortland exposes you to portfolio-level leasing patterns, application volume trends, and Fair Housing compliance in ways that on-site leasing roles often don't. If you're thinking about where a role like this leads, positions like Leasing Manager, Regional Leasing Director, or Operations Coordinator are natural next steps for someone who performs well here and wants to grow within a large multifamily platform.

greenhouse_5999989004.title: Regional Manager
greenhouse_5999989004.rewritten_description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Regional management at a third-party firm like Asset Living demands a different skill set than in-house portfolio work. You're accountable to ownership groups with varying expectations, reporting requirements, and asset classes, while simultaneously keeping your on-site teams aligned with a single company's operational standards. The skills that carry the most weight here: financial fluency at the portfolio level, the ability to read and redirect team performance without being on-site daily, and the judgment to balance owner priorities against consistent operational execution.

Atlanta's multifamily market gives this role a particular texture. The metro has absorbed significant new Class A supply over the past few years, which means concessions pressure and occupancy management are real, active concerns across many submarkets. A Regional Manager working a mixed portfolio here needs to know when to push rate and when to protect occupancy, and those decisions vary block by block. Asset Living's portfolio spans multifamily, single-family rentals, affordable housing, build-to-rent, and student housing nationally, so the Atlanta-based candidates who thrive here tend to have exposure across more than one asset class.

What the Work Actually Covers

Day-to-day, this role sits at the intersection of people management and financial oversight. You'll screen, hire, coach, and when necessary, separate on-site staff. That means building a paper trail, working closely with HR, and holding Community Managers accountable to performance benchmarks without micromanaging. You'll approve timesheets, sign off on salary requests, and make sure counseling documentation reaches the right hands before decisions escalate.

On the financial side, you'll own annual budget development and provide monthly written analysis of line items that drift materially from forecast. NOI improvement is the core objective, which involves both cost discipline and revenue strategy. You'll identify trends across the portfolio and recommend adjustments to leasing posture, pricing, or capex prioritization as conditions shift.

  • Develop and monitor yearly operating budgets and owner financial reports
  • Review and approve vendor invoices, proposals, and contracts for major projects
  • Build and execute annual marketing plans with site-level leasing strategies
  • Oversee emergency response protocols and ensure properties meet safety and fair housing standards
  • Conduct regular property inspections to track maintenance responsiveness and physical condition
  • Ensure lease documentation, reporting systems, and administrative processes are accurate and current

Resident retention also falls under this role's scope. That includes overseeing renewal strategy, resident programming, and how on-site teams handle complaints and service requests. In a market with real lease-up competition, retention is as important as traffic generation.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The candidates who do well in third-party Regional Manager roles aren't just operationally solid. They understand that each owner relationship is different and that communicating financial performance clearly to ownership is as important as the performance itself. If you've worked only in-house, that shift in accountability can take time to adjust to. Asset Living's AMO accreditation and NMHC top-50 standing signal that ownership reporting and fiduciary standards are taken seriously here.

Candidates who stand out will bring experience managing a portfolio that includes at least one non-conventional asset type, whether that's build-to-rent, student housing, or affordable. They'll also have handled a genuine performance management situation, not just coached strong performers, but documented and resolved underperformance through proper channels. That's where a lot of Regional Manager candidates have gaps, and it shows up quickly in this kind of role.

greenhouse_6000500004.title: Regional Manager
greenhouse_6000500004.rewritten_description:
Third-party management at scale creates a specific kind of regional role. Asset Living operates fee management across multifamily, single-family rentals, affordable housing, build-to-rent, and student housing, which means a Regional Manager here isn't overseeing one asset class or one owner. You're accountable to multiple clients, multiple property types, and a team spread across sites, all at once. That breadth is both the challenge and the draw.

What This Role Actually Covers

The short version: you run a portfolio. The longer version is that you're responsible for every function that touches that portfolio, from hiring and coaching on-site Community Managers to reviewing monthly financials and making sure NOI is moving in the right direction. You'll develop yearly operating budgets, write monthly variance explanations for income and expense lines that run over, and flag capex needs before they become emergencies. You'll also review and approve all salary requests, timesheets, and personnel actions across your sites.

On the leasing side, you'll build annual marketing plans, monitor traffic and closing rates, and step in when a site's occupancy or delinquency trends start heading the wrong direction. You're not doing the leasing yourself, but you're accountable for the results. If a site's staff isn't converting leads or following up properly, that's your problem to diagnose and fix.

Maintenance and administrative oversight are part of the job too. You'll conduct regular property inspections, keep an eye on service request turnaround times, review vendor bids and contracts for larger projects, and make sure financial close-out is completed accurately and on time for ownership reporting.

Who Fits This Role

  • Proven experience managing a multifamily portfolio as a regional or area manager
  • Solid financial fluency: budget development, variance analysis, NOI management
  • Experience hiring, coaching, and when necessary, separating on-site staff through proper documentation and HR process
  • Working knowledge of fair housing law and risk management responsibilities
  • Ability to manage multiple ownership relationships with different reporting expectations
  • Comfortable operating offsite from the properties you oversee

What separates strong candidates from average ones in a third-party management regional role is the ability to context-switch quickly. Your properties won't all have the same owner, the same asset class, or the same performance challenges. A regional who thrives here can read a T-12, shift to a delinquency conversation, then get on a call with an owner about a capex proposal, all in the same afternoon, without losing the thread on any of them. Candidates who've only managed a single-owner portfolio sometimes underestimate how much of this role is relationship management alongside operations.

This position is based in Sacramento, CA and reports into senior leadership. Asset Living holds IREM's Accredited Management Organization designation, which signals a baseline of operational standards you'll be expected to uphold and reinforce across your portfolio.

greenhouse_7740563003.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Business Manager role at Canopy at Citrus Park puts you in the seat where financial performance and people leadership intersect. On a given day, you might be reviewing T-12 trends with your Regional Manager in the morning, walking units with maintenance to confirm make-ready timelines before noon, and sitting down with a vendor to negotiate a service contract by mid-afternoon. This isn't a role where you hand things off and wait for reports. You're the one producing them, analyzing them, and then building strategy around what you find.

Occupancy, delinquency, NOI, renewal rates, concessions decisions: these metrics live on your desk. You'll build annual business plans and budget forecasts, supervise leasing and retention programs to hold maximum occupancy, and keep the asset in market-ready condition through regular property inspections. Your maintenance team looks to you for direction, your office staff looks to you for coaching, and your Regional VP looks to you for accountability.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of direct property manager experience in multifamily, with Class A or luxury lease-up experience genuinely preferred (Canopy at Citrus Park positions itself at that level)
  • Comfort reading and reporting financial performance, not just summarizing it
  • Hands-on experience with RealPage, OneSite, or Knock. Olympus lists these as strongly preferred, not optional in practice
  • A real track record of training and developing leasing staff, not just supervising them
  • Flexibility for after-hours resident events and emergency response when the situation calls for it

Where This Role Leads

Business Manager at a well-run, nationally recognized operator is one of the cleaner stepping stones into Regional Manager work. The skills that compound here are the ones that matter most at the next level: budget ownership, vendor contract management, and the ability to coach a team toward measurable results rather than just directing daily tasks. Olympus specifically offers career pathing resources and leadership conferences, which signals they're thinking about internal promotion, not just backfilling seats.

What separates strong candidates from average ones at this level usually isn't leasing knowledge. Most people applying have that. It's financial fluency combined with genuine coaching instinct. A manager who can identify why NOI is drifting and simultaneously develop the assistant manager who'll handle it next quarter is the one who moves up. If that describes how you already operate, this role is structured to reward it. Base pay starts at $80,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility on top of that.

greenhouse_7741897003.title: Leasing Consultant -  Olympus Auburn Lakes
greenhouse_7741897003.rewritten_description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Leasing is a conversion game. At Olympus Auburn Lakes in Spring, TX, the Leasing Consultant position puts two skill sets front and center: sales and service. Not one or the other. You're closing new leases while simultaneously keeping current residents happy enough to renew. Traffic-to-lease ratios matter here. So does your ability to read a prospect, match them to the right unit, and move paperwork efficiently. If you've spent time in hospitality, retail, or restaurants, you already know how to hold a room and recover from a tough interaction. That experience translates directly.

The base pay runs $18 to $20 per hour, and on top of that, the role carries monthly leasing commissions and renewal bonuses. In a well-run lease-up or stabilized community, those bonuses can meaningfully change your monthly take-home. Your renewal performance is just as financially relevant as your new leases.

What You're Actually Doing Day to Day

You're the first face most prospects see. That means greeting walk-ins, fielding calls and online leads, touring units, explaining floor plan differences, and asking for the commitment. Once a prospect says yes, you're handling the lease paperwork, coordinating move-in keys, and entering data into the resident database accurately. Administrative precision matters here because errors at the lease stage create downstream problems for the entire team.

Beyond leasing, you're helping plan and run resident events, visiting local businesses and locators to drive traffic back to the property, and responding to resident concerns with the kind of follow-through that supports renewals. Weekend availability is required, and some after-hours commitment for resident functions comes with the territory. That's the honest reality of a leasing role.

  • Minimum 1 year of apartment leasing experience, or comparable customer-facing sales background in hospitality, retail, or restaurants
  • Full-time schedule: Monday through Friday, rotating hours within 9 AM to 6 PM window
  • Saturday and Sunday availability required
  • Monthly after-hours availability for resident events

What Makes This Specific Opportunity Worth Considering

Olympus Property has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer recognition three consecutive years: 2023, 2024, and 2025. That's not a one-time survey result. Sustained recognition at that level usually reflects something real about how the company operates internally, how teams are supported, and how management treats site staff. For a Leasing Consultant early in a property management career, company culture affects how quickly you develop. Being surrounded by a team that shares leads, covers for each other, and actually collaborates makes you better at the job faster.

Strong candidates here aren't just energetic closers. They're people who genuinely track their own numbers, follow up consistently, and take resident retention as seriously as new traffic. The consultants who grow into leasing managers or assistant managers at companies like Olympus are the ones who treat every renewal as a sale and every resident interaction as a data point worth noting.

greenhouse_7942282.title: Assistant Property Manager
greenhouse_7942282.rewritten_description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, and that history shows up in how they actually run their communities. Headquartered in Richmond and operating more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia, this is a company that still takes a hands-on approach to daily operations. The Assistant Property Manager role at Bexley Village at Concord Mills reflects that culture directly: you're not a background player here. You're front-facing, involved in leasing, resident relations, and the day-to-day rhythm of the property.

Concord sits in the Charlotte metro's northeastern growth corridor, and the Concord Mills area carries solid residential demand from both the suburban sprawl and employment anchors nearby. That context matters for this role because traffic at a well-located garden-style community in this submarket tends to stay steady. You'll be working real leads, not waiting for the phone to ring.

On a typical day, you might start by responding to internet leads and scheduling tours, then shift into processing a leasing application or pulling together lease paperwork. Later in the afternoon you're walking a make-ready unit alongside maintenance to confirm it's ready before move-in, or sitting with a resident going over their renewal options. Delinquency follow-up, security deposit dispositions after move-outs, posting rent payments , all of it cycles through this role. You'll also help plan and host resident events, which is a smaller slice of the job but a meaningful one when it comes to retention.

Weinstein is open to candidates who don't have property management experience, and they mean it. If you've managed a front-of-house team, led a sales floor, or handled customer escalations in a hospitality environment, those skills transfer cleanly. What separates strong candidates here isn't a specific credential , it's the combination of genuine service instinct and the organizational discipline to manage multiple priorities without dropping details. The leasing and property operations side can be taught. The people skills and follow-through are harder to train.

The schedule runs weekdays 9 to 6, with Saturday hours on a team rotation. The role starts at $21 per hour with increases based on experience, quarterly bonuses, a sign-on bonus (details shared during the interview), and a benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, 401k with company match, rent discount, paid holidays, and birthday time off.

What the role requires

  • Some prior leadership or management experience, from any industry
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort working directly with the public, including in difficult or emotionally charged situations
  • Attention to detail in paperwork, lease processing, and unit inspections
  • Willingness to work occasional Saturdays and support resident events outside standard hours
  • Property management experience is a plus but not required

Many of Weinstein's current leaders started in leasing or assistant-level roles on-site. The career path here is real, whether that means growing into a property manager position or moving toward a regional or corporate track over time.

greenhouse_5141701007.title: Leasing Consultant- Farmers Branch, TX
greenhouse_5141701007.rewritten_description:
Leasing Consultant roles at apartment communities live and die on two things: how well you convert traffic into signed leases, and how well you keep current residents happy enough to renew. At MG Properties, a company with three decades of multifamily experience across the Western U.S., this position in Farmers Branch, TX covers both.

What the Job Actually Looks Like

Most of your day involves working with prospective residents. You'll greet people touring the property, qualify applicants, guide them through the lease signing process, and coordinate with maintenance to make sure move-ins go smoothly. That last part matters more than it sounds. A botched move-in kills goodwill fast, and a Leasing Consultant who stays on top of the punch list before a new resident walks through the door earns trust that carries through the lease term.

On the administrative side, you'll maintain rental files, enter data accurately into the property management system, and support monthly reporting tasks. You'll also be a first point of contact when current residents have maintenance concerns or payment questions. This isn't a sit-at-the-desk-and-wait role. You're actively managing the leasing pipeline and resident relationships at the same time.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management or related experience (preferred)
  • Strong sales instincts and the ability to close without being pushy
  • Customer service skills that hold up under pressure, including difficult conversations with residents
  • Professional communication, both written and verbal
  • Attention to detail on paperwork and lease files
  • Comfort working as part of a team and following a site's operational rhythm

Compensation and Growth

MG Properties offers monthly and quarterly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and a full benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and flexible spending accounts. PTO, paid holidays, personal days, and paid sick time are included. Rental discounts are also available.

The company promotes from within consistently. Leasing Consultant is a genuine entry point into property management careers. Strong performers here typically move into Senior Leasing roles or Assistant Manager positions, where they take on more of the financial and operational side of running a property. If you're early in your multifamily career and want a path forward, the trajectory is real here, not just a line in the job posting.

greenhouse_8557258002.title: Property Inspector
greenhouse_8557258002.rewritten_description:
Field-based property care roles in the short-term rental space sit at an interesting intersection: part inspector, part hospitality runner, part light maintenance coordinator. At Roofstock, this position sits inside a newly built STR business unit, which means the work carries real weight. Guest review scores, owner satisfaction, and the unit's ability to scale into new markets all trace back to what happens on the ground between stays.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll cover a defined zone of single-family homes in the Pacific City, Oregon market, moving between properties before and after guest stays. A typical shift involves pre-arrival inspections against brand standards, restocking consumables, resetting decor, handling punch list items like bulb swaps or TV resets, and documenting anything that needs escalation to the maintenance team. The role also pulls in some front-of-house work: responding to in-stay guest issues when dispatched, making outbound calls to guests or owners, and occasionally supporting the Hospitality Manager with task dispatching during off-peak hours.

The physical demands are real. You'll be on your feet most of the day, driving between properties, lifting up to 50 lbs, and staying available for urgent calls on weekends, holidays, and early mornings. The schedule is full-time with two days off per week, and the $22.50/hr rate is supplemented by a $135/month car allowance and $100/month for tools and equipment.

What the Role Requires

  • At least one year in hospitality, vacation rental operations, property care, or a closely related field
  • Comfort working from checklists and holding yourself to consistent brand standards
  • Strong communication skills and a service-first attitude when dealing with guests and owners
  • Ability to use mobile apps and task tracking tools reliably in the field
  • Valid driver's license, a dependable vehicle, and availability for weekend and on-call rotations
  • Physical capability to walk, stand, and lift throughout extended shifts

Where This Role Can Take You

The skills you build here compound in ways that aren't obvious at first. Conducting inspections against brand standards, tracking supply patterns, flagging recurring property issues, and managing guest relationships in real time are all transferable to property management roles in long-term rentals, make-ready coordination, and operations leadership. Because Roofstock's STR unit is in active growth mode, there's also an internal path: coordinators who demonstrate reliability and market knowledge tend to move into team lead, hospitality manager, or multi-zone operations roles as the business expands. In a company that's explicitly building this business unit from the ground up, early contributors tend to have more visibility than they would in a mature portfolio.

One honest note: this role rewards people who thrive on variety and self-direction in the field, but it can be demanding when urgent in-stay issues stack up on a holiday weekend. If you do your best work when no two shifts look alike, that's a signal this might be a strong fit.

greenhouse_8558003002.title: Community Manager
greenhouse_8558003002.location: FUSE, 720 Northwestern Ave, West Lafayette, IN,United States
greenhouse_8558003002.rewritten_description:
Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily, and this role reflects that. Scion's FUSE property in West Lafayette sits right in Purdue's orbit, which means the leasing calendar, the turn cycle, and the resident base all operate on an academic rhythm. The Community Manager (titled General Manager internally) is the person responsible for making that rhythm work, every day, across every department.

This isn't a light management role. You'll carry the full weight of financial performance, from building and defending the annual budget to tracking NOI, managing concessions, and hitting leasing velocity targets. You'll also own the annual turn, which in student housing is a concentrated, high-stakes operation. Moving furniture, walking units, running punch lists alongside the facilities team, coordinating vendors under tight deadlines , that hands-on expectation is written directly into the job. If you've only managed turn from a spreadsheet, this role will stretch you.

Day-to-day, you're toggling between the operational and the interpersonal. One hour you're reviewing variance reports or approving vendor bids. The next you're de-escalating a resident concern your AGM has escalated to you, or you're walking the property to complete a monthly scorecard assessment. After-hours on-call responsibility comes with the position. That's not buried in fine print here , Scion lists it plainly, and it's worth taking seriously when you consider fit.

Staff development is a real part of the job, not a line item. You'll partner with HR and talent acquisition to hire through Greenhouse, then work with L&D to build a team that can actually operate the property without you hovering. High morale on a student housing site isn't automatic , the seasonal pressure is real, the resident population turns over every year, and keeping your team motivated through a summer turn cycle takes deliberate effort.

What the role requires

  • At least 3 years managing a residential community with a team of three or more direct reports
  • Comfort working in property management software, with Entrata experience preferred
  • Familiarity with budgeting, payroll, invoice processing, and month-end close processes
  • Strong conflict management skills , with residents, vendors, and staff
  • Ability to work non-traditional hours during peak periods, emergencies, and weather events
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Scion uses a specific tech stack , Vena for budgeting, Entrata for property management, Lattice for performance, Turnable for the electronic turn board, and ClickUp for project tracking. You don't need to know all of them on day one, but candidates who pick up new platforms quickly will move faster here.

Where this role leads: Community Managers in student housing who develop strong financial fluency and a track record of clean turns tend to move into regional or portfolio-level positions. The operational complexity of student housing, with its compressed timelines and high resident turnover, builds instincts that translate well into conventional multifamily and fee management environments too.

Compensation includes a discretionary annual bonus, health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental and maternal leave, paid time off, and learning reimbursement. The position is exempt and based on-site at FUSE, 720 Northwestern Ave, West Lafayette.

greenhouse_4250507009.title: Maintenance Technician (414 Petaluma)
greenhouse_4250507009.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work at an affordable housing community asks something different of you than a typical apartment job. The residents here aren't just tenants. They're working families, seniors, and people with special needs who depend on their home being safe and functional in ways that go beyond inconvenience. That context shapes every work order, every turn, every time you pick up a call at 11pm.

The Skills This Role Runs On

This isn't a groundskeeper role with some light repairs mixed in. MidPen is looking for someone with genuine depth across electrical, plumbing, and carpentry. That means diagnosing a tripped circuit or a failing fixture, not just replacing a light bulb. It means handling plumbing repairs at the water and sewage system level, not just unclogging drains. Rough and finish carpentry both matter here, because a unit that's been turned needs to look right and hold up, not just pass a quick walk-through.

Landscaping and irrigation round out the technical picture. You'll maintain grounds and lighting to MidPen's standards, which at an affordable housing community also means keeping common areas clean, well-lit, and secure. That's not incidental. It's part of what makes the property feel like a home.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A lot of your time will be split between reactive work orders and scheduled preventive maintenance. Turns are part of the rhythm too: when a unit goes vacant, you're responsible for getting it make-ready within established timeframes, which covers painting, flooring, fixtures, and appliances. You'll coordinate with outside contractors on some jobs, helping with bid reviews, scheduling, and making sure the work actually gets done to standard.

You'll also carry a mentorship responsibility. The Maintenance Groundskeeper staff reports below this role, and MidPen expects you to coach and develop that team, not just supervise it. If you've never trained anyone before, that part of the job will take some adjustment.

The on-call rotation is real and worth understanding clearly. You'll cover a full seven-day rotating on-call stretch, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. Emergency calls during those windows aren't optional. That's the honest version of what "24/7 support" means in practice.

What Makes This Role at MidPen Different

MidPen has operated affordable housing across more than 130 properties in Northern California since 1970. They're not a startup figuring out property management. The structure here, the preventive maintenance schedules, the work order documentation requirements, the procurement processes, reflects an organization that's been doing this long enough to build real systems.

Pay runs $25.00 to $28.13 hourly depending on experience. Bilingual ability in English and Spanish is preferred, and at a Petaluma property serving a diverse resident population, that preference has practical weight in daily interactions.

  • Three or more years of maintenance experience, with property management background preferred
  • Strong plumbing and electrical knowledge at a systems level, not just surface repairs
  • Rough and finish carpentry skills
  • Basic OSHA awareness and landscape maintenance familiarity
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds regularly and work in all weather and physical conditions
  • Computer skills sufficient for work order systems and documentation
  • High school diploma or GED required

Strong candidates here tend to be the ones who already think in terms of documentation and follow-through, not just fixing the problem in front of them. A work order that gets completed but not closed out, or a contractor job that gets scheduled but not followed up on, creates gaps that compound over time at a property this size. The technical skills get you in the door. The organizational habits are what make you effective here long-term.

It's a Tuesday morning and your delinquency report is already open, a vendor is waiting on an approval, and one of your leasing consultants needs coaching before a tour at 11. That's not a bad day. That's just the job.

Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Community Manager for a property on Green Valley Road in Greensboro, NC. Hawthorne ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies in the country, with a footprint rooted in the Southeast. This is a full operational leadership role. You're responsible for the financial performance, team development, leasing results, resident satisfaction, and physical condition of the community. You report to regional leadership and ownership groups, which means your numbers and your culture both need to be in order.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're managing budget performance, overseeing rent collection, tracking delinquency, and handling deposit accounting at move-out. You'll run weekly team meetings, conduct property inspections, manage vendor relationships, and stay on top of work orders alongside your maintenance team. Leasing doesn't stop being your concern when you step into this seat. You'll support traffic, guide renewals, set pricing strategy to protect occupancy, and make sure lease documents are completed accurately and on time. You'll also manage the community's online reputation, respond to reviews, and handle escalated resident concerns that your team can't resolve on their own.

Yardi and Knock are the platforms Hawthorne uses. Comfort with both is preferred. If you've read a T-12 and made a budget decision from it, that experience matters here.

The office schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays from 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep hours at 40. Resident events and community needs can pull you outside those hours occasionally. That's worth knowing going in.

Compensation includes a base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and telehealth access.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role from average ones: the ability to hold a team accountable without losing their trust. Coaching a leasing consultant through a slow traffic week while keeping morale intact and still hitting your occupancy number is a real skill. If you've done that before, you already know what Hawthorne is looking for.

greenhouse_4252953009.title: Recertification Specialist
greenhouse_4252953009.rewritten_description:
Affordable housing compliance runs on paperwork, deadlines, and a very specific kind of attention to detail. Recertification is the annual (or more frequent) process that keeps income-restricted residents in compliance with HUD, LIHTC, or other program requirements. When it slips, properties face findings, corrective action plans, and potential funding risk. This role exists to keep that process moving cleanly at Westcott Terrace in West Warwick, RI.

What This Role Actually Involves

John M. Corcoran and Company, a New England real estate firm operating since 1951, is hiring a part-time Recertification Specialist at roughly 20 hours per week. Eight of those hours fall on Saturday, with the remaining hours scheduled flexibly across other days. That Saturday requirement is worth thinking through before you apply. It's a real commitment, even at part-time volume.

The core work centers on the tenant recertification cycle: scheduling interviews with residents, collecting documentation, maintaining compliant resident files, and coordinating apartment inspections tied to recertification. You'll also support waitlist management and applicant processing, which adds another layer of regulatory care. Beyond the compliance-specific work, you'll pitch in on general office tasks when needed, including rent collection, phones, maintenance request intake, and resident event support.

The pay range runs from $25.75 to $31.00 per hour, and there's a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off, holidays, and a 401(k) with company match.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least two years in an administrative role, ideally one with regulatory or compliance documentation
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills. You'll be working directly with residents who may be anxious about the recertification process
  • Organized enough to track multiple files at different stages of the certification cycle simultaneously
  • Comfortable with property management or compliance software
  • Familiarity with affordable housing regulations (HUD, LIHTC, or similar) is a genuine advantage here, not just a nice-to-have

What separates a strong candidate from an average one in this role is the ability to handle residents who are stressed or confused about what they need to provide. Recertification interviews can surface sensitive household information. Residents sometimes push back, go quiet, or miss deadlines. The person who does this job well stays organized under that friction, communicates clearly without being cold, and doesn't let one difficult interaction back up the whole pipeline.

If you're building a career in affordable housing compliance, this role gives you direct exposure to the recertification workflow at an established firm. That experience translates well toward housing compliance coordinator or property manager roles at affordable communities, where recertification knowledge is increasingly specialized and in demand.

greenhouse_5225043008.title: Maintenance Technician 2 - Britton Woods Apartments
greenhouse_5225043008.rewritten_description:
It's 7:30 on a Tuesday morning and a resident has already called in a leak under their kitchen sink. By 9:00, you're halfway through a make-ready in a vacant unit, patching drywall before the painter comes through. That's the rhythm at Britton Woods.

The Role at Britton Woods Apartments

Ackermann Group, a Midwest real estate and property management company with roots going back to 1938, is hiring a full-time Maintenance Technician 2 for Britton Woods Apartments, a 352-unit community in Dublin, Ohio. This is a training-level role, which means you're expected to bring at least a year of general maintenance experience to the table, but you'll also have room to build real proficiency across multiple trade areas over time.

Day-to-day, the work covers a wide range. You'll handle unit make-readies, working through punch lists to get vacants rent-ready. You'll respond to service requests that range from basic to intermediate, including plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliance repair, HVAC, and painting. Exterior grounds upkeep, janitorial duties, pool water management when applicable, and participation in preventative maintenance rounds all fall within scope. When snow events hit central Ohio (and they do), you're part of the prep and removal crew. You'll also take part in move-in and move-out inspections alongside your supervisor.

The on-call rotation is real. After-hours emergency calls are part of the job, and it's worth being honest about that. The rotation spreads the load across the team, but you should expect some nights and weekends when it's your turn. If that's a dealbreaker, this role isn't the right fit. If you're already used to it, you know it comes with the territory.

What This Role Calls For

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience with demonstrated range across general trades
  • Valid driver's license with proof of insurance
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • EPA Type I and II, CAMT, or CPO certifications are a plus but not required
  • Strong attention to detail, especially when working through make-ready punch lists
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 8:00am to 5:00pm, plus participation in the after-hours emergency on-call rotation

What separates a strong candidate here isn't just technical skill. It's the ability to manage a shifting workload without dropping the ball on the details. A make-ready that looks done but has a running toilet or a sticky cabinet door creates a bad first impression for an incoming resident. The technicians who do well in roles like this one catch those things before anyone else has to point them out.

Ackermann offers competitive hourly pay with quarterly bonus potential and lease renewal commission, health benefits including medical, dental, and vision, a 401k with company match, paid time off that includes your birthday, an employee rent discount at any Ackermann community, and career coaching and development support. For someone looking to grow within the maintenance trade, the structured training component of this role is a genuine asset.

greenhouse_4683075006.rewritten_description:
This role lives and dies on soft skills. Before you think about property management knowledge or tech systems, consider the abilities that actually drive performance here: reading a room quickly, staying composed when multiple things demand your attention at once, and making people feel genuinely welcomed rather than processed. The Reside Living Concierge position at River West is built around those capabilities first.

The Work Itself

Your shift runs either Monday overnight (11:30 PM to 7:30 AM) or Thursday through Sunday on second shift (3:30 PM to midnight), with Tuesday and Wednesday off. That schedule matters because it shapes who you're serving and how. Overnight and late evening hours mean you're often the only Reside representative a resident or prospect interacts with. You're greeting guests, answering the concierge station phones, coordinating transportation requests, and handling walk-in traffic with rental information. When the leasing offices are closed, rollover calls from across Reside's Chicago portfolio come to you, so your ability to communicate clearly and stay organized under pressure carries real weight.

Beyond the front-of-house work, you're also the after-hours link to property management. Resident emergencies, maintenance dispatching, service request intake, and follow-up calls all fall within your scope. You'll monitor security systems and cameras, manage entries in CFR systems, and assist with resident events and social functions at various properties. It's a genuinely varied role, and the variety is the point.

Skills That Carry You Through

Reside is looking for at least one year of customer-facing experience, ideally in hospitality, luxury retail, or a service-oriented setting. Property management or leasing background is a plus but not required. What actually distinguishes strong candidates here is less about industry knowledge and more about communication instincts: the ability to solve a problem through conversation, to stay organized when the phone is ringing and a resident is standing at the desk, and to follow through on small details like a follow-up call after a completed service request. Those details are what residents actually remember.

  • One year or more of customer-facing experience in hospitality, retail, or luxury services
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint)
  • Organizational skills and genuine attention to detail
  • Ability to work independently during overnight hours while staying engaged with the team
  • Physical ability to stand and move for the majority of the shift, climb stairs, and carry items under 20 lbs. regularly

What Working at Reside Looks Like

Reside Living manages around 3,000 apartments across Chicago and is actively growing. The company positions its properties as modern, amenity-forward communities, and the Concierge program is central to that identity. You're not just staffing a desk; you're part of what separates a Reside building from a generic rental. That means the role gets taken seriously internally, which tends to translate into real career development for people who want it. Concierge experience at a company like this builds a strong foundation for moving into leasing or assistant community manager roles over time.

Compensation starts at $20.00 per hour. Benefits include medical, dental, life, and disability insurance, a 401K with matching, commuter benefits, paid time off starting at 13 days (increasing after year one), paid holidays, a 25% monthly apartment discount, $100 per month in student loan assistance, and a $750 career apparel allowance after 90 days.

greenhouse_6000269004.rewritten_description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a hands-on maintenance technician role at Lake St. James Apartments in Conyers, GA, a residential community managed by Cottonwood Residential. The work covers the full range of apartment maintenance: plumbing repairs, electrical work, general carpentry, make-ready turns, and responding to service requests across the property. You'll also carry on-call responsibilities, meaning after-hours emergencies are part of the job. The Service Manager supports you on those calls, but you need to be the kind of person who can handle an urgent situation at 10pm without falling apart.

Physical demands here are real. You're on your feet most of the day, climbing stairs, working in tight spaces, lifting up to 50 lbs, and occasionally on ladders or scaffolding. If you've worked apartment maintenance before, none of that surprises you. If you haven't, it's worth knowing before you apply.

A typical week might include a handful of work orders (plumbing calls, HVAC filter swaps, appliance issues), contributing to unit turns between residents, and keeping an eye on the property grounds. Punch lists don't manage themselves, and in a busy community, the backlog can build fast if you're not organized.

What You Bring

  • Experience with plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry repairs in a residential setting
  • A valid driver's license
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (a real plus, not just a nice-to-have if you want to stand out)
  • CPO certification (helpful if the property has a pool)
  • Ability to communicate clearly with residents and document work orders accurately
  • Willingness to work evenings, weekends, and rotating on-call shifts

Strong candidates in this kind of role tend to be self-starters who don't need someone walking them through every work order. They communicate proactively when a repair turns into something bigger than expected, and they understand that a resident waiting on a fix is having a worse day than you are. That mindset matters more than any single certification.

The Role in Context

Cottonwood Residential has built a reputation around a self-guided tour model that puts resident experience at the center of operations. That culture extends to maintenance. A fast, quality repair done with a decent attitude does more for retention than most marketing. If you're the technician residents trust, you'll feel that in the job.

greenhouse_8558704002.title: Assistant Community Manager
greenhouse_8558704002.rewritten_description:
Waypoint Management Services is building something worth joining in Davenport, FL, and they need an Assistant Community Manager who's ready to show up, own their piece of the operation, and genuinely invest in the people around them.

This role sits right at the intersection of relationships and results. You'll work alongside the Community Manager on just about everything that keeps a multifamily community running well: supporting the leasing team, monitoring delinquency, tracking renewals and make-ready schedules, and making sure the rent roll and resident records stay accurate. Financial reporting and occupancy management are part of the daily rhythm here, not just occasional tasks. You'll also weigh in on pricing recommendations based on market surveys and what occupancy is doing, which means you need to be comfortable reading the numbers and speaking to them.

On the people side, this job asks a lot. You're coaching leasing staff, fielding resident concerns, managing vendor relationships, and staying sharp on what competitors in the area are doing. Weekend availability is required, and that's worth being honest about: the best candidate for this role won't just tolerate that schedule, they'll understand that multifamily communities don't pause on Saturdays.

Where this role tends to lead is worth considering. ACMs who develop strong financial instincts alongside their people skills move into Community Manager seats faster than those who stay on just one side of the job. If you can sit in a budget conversation and a resident retention discussion with equal confidence, you're building a profile that translates well to solo portfolio ownership down the road.

What you'll bring

  • At least two years of experience in leasing, sales, or a hospitality setting
  • Comfort with financial basics: collections, delinquency management, and reporting
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including digital and social channels
  • Yardi experience is a plus, though not a hard requirement
  • High school diploma or equivalent, plus a valid driver's license
  • Availability to work weekend rotations

Waypoint offers a benefits package that starts on day one, including medical, dental, and vision coverage. You'll also get PTO from the start, a 401k with company match, leasing and renewal bonuses, an employee housing discount, and access to professional development. These aren't afterthoughts here; they're part of how the company signals that it wants people to stay and grow.

If you've been in a leasing role and you're ready to step into something with more operational weight and more visibility, this is a reasonable next move. The job has real breadth, and the right person will find that energizing rather than scattered.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

A typical shift starts with a scan of open work orders, a walk of the grounds, and a check on any units in make-ready status. You might spend the morning completing a punch list on a vacant unit , appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry , and the afternoon handling resident service requests that came in overnight. You're also the eyes on the property: if something looks off on a curb appeal walk, you flag it or fix it before management hears about it from a prospective resident on a tour.

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions move faster and accountability runs deeper than at a third-party management shop. Equipment care and supply tracking are part of the job, not an afterthought.

Technicians who develop a broad skill set across trades , especially HVAC, electrical, and plumbing , tend to move into Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor roles within a few years. At a company that manages its own portfolio, those promotions happen from within more consistently than at fee management organizations where staffing decisions can shift with contract renewals. lever_2c60cee0-a440-4ecd-8f87-7da34478a3.title: Experienced Field Maintenance Technician (3+ Years Required)
lever_2c60cee0-a440-4ecd-8f87-7da34478a3.rewritten_description:
Third-party property services at scale work differently than site-based maintenance. Instead of owning one asset, you own a territory of work orders across a portfolio, which means your diagnostic speed, vendor coordination instincts, and budget awareness compound faster than they would managing a single property. That's the environment Lessen operates in, and it's the environment this role is built for.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Lessen handles maintenance across more than one million properties, completing north of 3.5 million work orders annually through a vetted affiliate network. As a Field Maintenance Technician in Denver, you're not cycling through the same hallways every day. You're moving across a portfolio, owning each work order from diagnosis to close-out, managing scope against budget, and making judgment calls in the field without a supervisor down the hall. The company emphasizes quality over ticket volume, which is a meaningful distinction. It means your decisions on materials, methods, and timing actually matter to client satisfaction metrics, not just throughput numbers.

Lessen provides a company vehicle with a fuel card, a monthly tool allowance, and a cell phone allowance, so the logistics of field work are covered. The schedule runs weekdays with no on-call rotation, which is genuinely uncommon in property maintenance and worth weighing against roles that pull you in nights and weekends. OSHA training is provided. There's a sign-on bonus opportunity and a quarterly discretionary bonus of up to 5% of quarterly earnings on top of the base hourly rate, which starts at $23 and goes to $27 depending on experience, skill level, and competencies.

Who Moves Up From Here

Lessen has mapped out a clear internal track toward Lead Technician and Field Maintenance Manager as the company expands nationally. That path is worth thinking about concretely. The skills that make someone effective in this role, specifically portfolio-level thinking, budget ownership, and the ability to triage across multiple property types without constant direction, are exactly what feed into a Lead or Manager role in third-party and fee management environments. Technicians who've only worked single-site or in-house often have to rebuild those habits when they step into multi-portfolio oversight. Starting here accelerates that curve.

To be competitive, you'll need at least three years of verifiable hands-on experience in property maintenance or a related trade. Lessen is explicit that they want solution-oriented technicians who can work independently and think forward, not just execute a punch list. If you've spent time in make-ready work, capex projects, or multi-property field roles, that background translates directly. Strong candidates typically combine real trade competency with the communication habits that keep clients informed and work orders moving without hand-holding.

  • Minimum 3 years of hands-on property maintenance or trade experience required
  • Ability to own work orders independently and manage job-level budgets
  • Comfort working across a portfolio of properties rather than a single site
  • Solution-oriented approach with an eye toward client outcomes, not just task completion

greenhouse_5224982008.rewritten_description:
A resident submits a ticket at 7 a.m.: no heat. By 8, you've diagnosed a failed blower motor, sourced the part, and updated the resident. That's the pace here.

Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager for a property in Atlanta's 30309 corridor. This is a hands-on supervisory role. You'll split your time between turning wrenches and leading a small maintenance team, and you need to be credible at both.

What the Job Covers

The core of this role is asset preservation and resident service. Day to day, that means resolving HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance issues, managing the make-ready process so turns stay on schedule, and running a preventative maintenance program that keeps the property from deteriorating between capex cycles. You'll also own general upkeep, grounds maintenance, and safety compliance across the building.

You'll work weekends and participate in the emergency on-call rotation. That's not a footnote; it's a real part of the job.

What You Bring

  • 5 or more years of experience in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems (central plant, boilers, chillers, split systems) is a plus
  • Knowledge of OSHA standards, risk management, and MSDS
  • Supervisory or team lead experience preferred
  • Comfort with technology platforms, work order software, and basic Microsoft Office tools
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in variable weather

The salary range is $60,000 to $70,000, with bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One thing that separates strong candidates here: they treat preventative maintenance as seriously as emergency repairs. Anyone can respond to a broken HVAC unit. The people who advance in this type of role are the ones who keep the failures from happening in the first place, and who build that discipline into the team around them. If your PM logs are always current and your team knows why, you'll fit well.

greenhouse_5227499008.rewritten_description:
Maintenance work at this level is half technical skill and half people management. You're not just fixing things. You're training others to fix things correctly, holding standards on punch lists, keeping turns moving, and making sure the preventative maintenance program actually gets executed rather than just scheduled. If that combination sounds like your day, this role fits.

What This Role Demands Technically

Bozzuto is looking for someone with 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance. The core technical work covers HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair, along with basic carpentry, drywall, and painting. Exposure to complex mechanical systems, such as central plant, split systems, boilers, and chillers, is a plus. An EPA and/or HVAC certification is expected, and NAPE is mentioned as well. You'll need to know OSHA standards, MSDS protocols, and how to run an operation where safety codes are treated as non-negotiable, not optional paperwork.

The make-ready process sits at the center of this role's operational impact. Turns need to be tight and thorough. A unit that sits down longer than it should costs the property real money, and a sloppy make-ready creates resident complaints before the new lease even starts. Attention to detail on punch lists isn't a soft skill here. It's a direct driver of occupancy and resident satisfaction.

The Leadership Side People Underestimate

This is an assistant manager position, which means you're setting the standard for how the maintenance team works and carries itself. Leading by example is listed as a primary responsibility, and that's not filler language. On a well-run property, the maintenance team's attitude toward residents shows up in every service ticket response, every hallway interaction, every emergency call handled at 11 PM. The on-call rotation and weekend availability are part of the job. That's honest. After-hours calls happen, and someone has to take them.

Strong candidates will have some supervisory experience, not just years of technical work. The ability to communicate clearly in writing and verbally matters too, because you'll be coordinating with leasing, management, and vendors, not just your own crew.

What It Looks Like at Bozzuto Specifically

Bozzuto manages a large portfolio of residential properties across the DC metro area, including some of the more architecturally complex and amenity-heavy communities in the region. That means the mechanical systems here tend to be more involved than what you'd find at a basic garden-style property. If you've only worked smaller or simpler assets, the learning curve on central plant systems is real.

The salary for this position is listed at $70,500 with bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. Career-wise, this role is a natural step toward a full Maintenance Manager or Director of Facilities position, particularly within a company that promotes from within as consistently as Bozzuto does.

  • EPA, HVAC, and/or NAPE certification

  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Ability to handle physical demands including lifting up to 50 pounds, ladder use, and outdoor work in varying weather
  • Availability for on-call emergencies and weekend shifts

greenhouse_7743248003.title: Business Manager - The Lock at Flatirons
greenhouse_7743248003.rewritten_description:
Property management has always had a clear dividing line between those who execute and those who lead. The Business Manager role at Olympus Property's The Lock at Flatirons sits firmly on the leadership side of that line. You're not just running a property. You're running a business unit, which means owning the numbers, developing a team, and making judgment calls that directly affect asset performance and resident experience.

The Scope of the Role

The Lock at Flatirons is a Class A community in Broomfield, CO, and this position carries the full weight of site-level leadership. Budget creation, NOI performance, occupancy management, delinquency oversight, vendor contract negotiation, and capex coordination all land on your desk. You'll work closely with a Regional Manager and Regional VP to build and execute annual business plans, which means you're expected to speak fluently about T-12 performance, monthly budget projections, and leasing trends, not just report them but analyze them and bring strategy to the conversation.

On the people side, you'll manage both office and maintenance staff. That dual responsibility is significant. Strong candidates in this role understand that a well-run make-ready program and a high-performing leasing team are two sides of the same occupancy equation. You'll mentor your office team on sales and marketing execution while providing direction to maintenance on inspections, unit conditions, and market-ready standards. Resident retention, renewal programs, and community events also fall within your scope, including flexibility for after-hours situations when they arise.

  • Minimum two years of experience as a property manager in multifamily, with Class A experience preferred
  • Familiarity with RealPage, Knock, and/or Onesite is strongly preferred
  • Full-time availability Monday through Friday, with schedule flexibility between 8 AM and 6 PM
  • Comfort with after-hours resident events and occasional emergencies

Where This Role Can Take You

Business Manager is one of the most skill-dense positions in multifamily because the job forces you to build competency in areas that most other roles only touch. You're reading financials, managing vendor relationships, coaching people, and driving leasing strategy simultaneously. That breadth is what makes this role a natural launchpad into Regional Manager or Portfolio Manager positions. Olympus specifically offers structured career pathing, leadership conferences, and what they call Budget Camp, which is a real signal that they invest in developing site-level leaders into regional ones rather than hiring from outside.
